body_fields.why: The graph must key each node on the agent-visible accesskit node of this tree, as the snapshot builds it, never on a DOM element.

body_fields.why: The graph reader, the signal registry and the snapshot field must reach seven_guis through the feature's existing edge, and no platform adapter may join the stand's graph.
body_fields.quote: `accessibility` is a default feature of both Dioxus crates; dioxus-native-dom's forwards to blitz-dom and enables its own optional `accesskit`, and dioxus-native's forwards to blitz-dom, blitz-shell and dioxus-native-dom (packages/dioxus-native-dom/Cargo.toml:13; packages/dioxus-native-dom/Cargo.toml:18; packages/dioxus-native-dom/Cargo.toml:41; packages/dioxus-native/Cargo.toml:13; packages/dioxus-native/Cargo.toml:32); the workspace takes both with `default-features = false`, so a crate gets the feature only by naming it or by depending on a crate that names it — the seven_guis stand binary names none in its own manifest and builds no platform adapter

`accessibility` is a default feature of both Dioxus crates, which the workspace takes with `default-features = false`; it reaches seven_guis through `escher-driver`, which names it unconditionally, while seven_guis' own manifest names none, and no stand binary builds a platform adapter, so no assistive technology is given a tree by the stand binary

body_fields.why: Moving the stand's signals onto the registry must leave the served pages keyed, `unkeyed_actionable` empty and their stated Tab sequences walking as stated.

body_fields.why: A test file the plan adds to the `a11y` leg, or a change to the published reach, must be written into the capability statement by hand, its count of files moved with it.
body_fields.quote: `docs/capabilities.md` («What Escher can do») publishes the accessibility reach under `## Accessibility reach`: tier 0, SC 2.1.1 · 1.4.3 · 2.4.3 and no other criterion, the `a11y` leg's fourteen files with no required status check, what an assistive technology reads unmeasured, and the named limits (the focus fixup firing no `blur`, a single select's `size` unread, `aria-activedescendant` unread); its pin `.github/scripts/test_capability_statement.py` reads none of these claims, so a change to the reach is made in that document by hand

body_fields.why: The graph must read the tree through the `Document::accessibility_tree` override carrying stable ids, the same nodes the snapshot and the platform tree consume.
body_fields.quote: both paths go through the `Document::accessibility_tree` trait method, so a wrapper's override (DioxusDocument's stable ids) reaches the platform tree
both paths through the `Document::accessibility_tree` trait method, so a wrapper's override (DioxusDocument's stable ids) reaches it; proven headlessly on the stand in both layout modes

body_fields.why: The new snapshot field and the graph reader must sit behind dioxus-native-dom's `accessibility` feature with the snapshot model, and the crate doc must name what that feature now gates.
body_fields.quote: dioxus-native-dom's feature also gates its own `accessibility_tree` override, its snapshot model (`DioxusDocument::snapshot`), that model's text form (`Snapshot::to_text`) and its parts (`Snapshot::text_parts`), its diff (`Snapshot::diff`) and its actionable-key check (`DioxusDocument::unkeyed_actionable`), all five of which its crate doc names

body_fields.why: No log site, span field or print of the graph may carry a node, a component name, a handler, a state or a value, the allowlist's redaction of `text` and `value` naming none of the graph's new content.
body_fields.quote: both behind a target allowlist that, among others, prints only `node_id` / `status` / `waiting_nodes` / `property` / `log.*` fields for `blitz*` and `accesskit_xplat` targets, redacts `text`, `value`, `html` and `attrs` for escher's own targets (`escher_*`) and drops a record from any other target whole, at every level — a closed span's every pair judged by the same rule, an outside target's span writing nothing

Native element mapping follows HTML-AAM: landmarks, headings, lists, tables, interactive and inline semantics (packages/blitz-dom/src/accessibility.rs:467-536)

body_fields.quote: **ARIA `role` attribute** — `role_from_name` maps ARIA role names (alert, button, checkbox, dialog, link, tab, textbox, landmark roles, etc.) to AccessKit roles (packages/blitz-dom/src/accessibility.rs:357-420)

body_fields.why: The «reacts to a click» field must report a disabled form control by the same presence-keyed gate the click path reads, so a control the click walk stops never reads as reacting.
body_fields.quote: the `DISABLED`/`ENABLED` element state (hence `:disabled`) reads the attribute's PRESENCE, and the pointer-move gate, `ClickTarget::Disabled`, `handle_click`'s walk gate, the Enter and Space activation and focusability read `ElementData::is_disabled` — that presence on a `button`, `input`, `select` or `textarea` alone (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18) — so `disabled="false"` and a bare `disabled=""` on a form control match `:disabled` and are not focusable
`button`, `input`, `select` and `textarea` can be disabled, which toggles the `DISABLED`/`ENABLED` states

Disabled-ness is keyed one way: the `DISABLED`/`ENABLED` state (hence `:disabled`), the pointer gates, Enter and Space activation and focusability read the `disabled` attribute's presence on a `button`, `input`, `select` or `textarea`

body_fields.why: The plan must settle whether a native button's own click activation, with no app handler, counts as reacting to a click, and keep a disabled form control and a click on any other element reading as the engine treats them.
body_fields.quote: A pointer click on a `button` (any type) or an `input` of type `submit`, `reset` or `button` focuses it through `generate_focus_events` / `set_focus_to`, then submits the form owner when it is a submit button, and ends the walk matched — since 2026-10-13-stand-keyboard-harness, in every document; before it a submit button submitted without breaking the walk and every other button fell through to the unmatched clear of focus, so an accepted click on one left no element focused (as measured at escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-10-scrolling-box-bounds-and-hit/report.md); a disabled form control still stops the walk first, a disabled ancestor `div` not (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18), and a click on any other element is unchanged — a CRUD row or the list still clears focus

A pointer click on a `button` or an `input` of type `submit`, `reset` or `button` focuses it, submits the form owner when it is a submit button and ends the walk, and a click on a single `select` focuses it and opens its list or closes one standing, each of two clicks on one point focusing; a click on a row of an open list chooses it, a disabled row changing nothing and leaving the list open and a group header choosing nothing; a press outside the list closes it with no event; a label's click on a bound single select focuses it and opens nothing; a click on a `multiple` select focuses it, a click on a `multiple` select's row focuses the select and acts on the row, and an option of a closed single select takes no click; a disabled form control stops the walk first, a disabled ancestor `div` not; a click on any other element is unchanged — a CRUD row or the list still clears focus.

body_fields.why: The new field must read a select and its options as the engine's click path treats them, a disabled select and an option of a closed single select reacting to no click.
body_fields.quote: A click on a `select` focuses it through `generate_focus_events` / `set_focus_to`, clearing its typeahead and the document's text selection, a disabled select stopped by the walk's gate first so it neither focuses nor acts; on a single select each click also opens its list or closes one standing, two clicks on one point opening then closing, each focusing, and a row of an open list takes a click through `handle_click`'s `option` arm behind `click_lands_on_row`, while an option of a closed single select, under a group too, is not clicked (a driver `click` on one is refused `covered` — on the stand the flight booker's two options among them)

body_fields.why: A `multiple` select's row reacts to a click through its own arm, and the new field must classify such a row, and a disabled one, consistently with that path.
body_fields.quote: A click on a `multiple` select's row runs `click_select_row` behind `handle_click`'s `option` arm, in every document: a disabled select stops it; otherwise it focuses the select and clears the typeahead and the text selection, a plain click chooses the row alone, Ctrl or Meta flips it, Shift spans, and a disabled row changes nothing

body_fields.why: A disabled row, or a disabled, inert, hidden or empty select, reacts to no click, and the new field must not report it as reacting.
body_fields.quote: A disabled row of an open list changes nothing and leaves the list open; a disabled, inert or hidden select, or one with no row to show, opens nothing

body_fields.why: A `summary` reacts to a click natively with no app handler, and the plan must decide whether the new field counts that.
body_fields.quote: Activating the first `summary` of a `details` toggles it open and focuses the summary
activating a `details`'s first `summary` (above) toggles `open` through the mutator and so flips `:open`

body_fields.why: Checkbox and radio clicks act natively, and the new field must state whether that native reaction counts beside a registered app handler.
body_fields.quote: Checkbox and radio clicks toggle state, dispatch `input` and move focus to the control

the list `crud-list`, named `People`, is the third CRUD Tab stop and, focused, ArrowDown / ArrowUp / Home / End move the selection as a row's click does

the arrows move `current`, clamped, and bring the cell into view; Enter opens the editor on `current`, focused, and the editor's Enter commits and returns focus to the grid; Tab leaving an open editor commits it

body_fields.quote: and the elements that react to input and state no interactive role are counted on the stand, in both layout modes, and pinned as measured — 0 on the four lean tasks, Home and Temperature Converter, Circle Drawer 1, Cells 677, the 676 data cells and `cells-grid` (`stand_non_lean_tasks::elements_that_react_to_a_click_and_state_no_role_are_counted`); no snapshot field says that an element reacts to a click (`NODE_FIELDS` thirteen) — that reading measured by link 2, its snapshot field owed to the route entry «The UI graph» on the founder's C3 «Замерить сейчас, поле позже (Рекомендую)» (2026-10-14), this count its starting reading

The actionable-key rule: every element an agent can act on — focusable, or carrying an interactive role, or carrying an event listener — reads an author key, so its `author_id` is that key and holds under any edit of the code around it (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-06); under dioxus-native-dom's `accessibility` feature `DioxusDocument::unkeyed_actionable` is the check — it reads focusability from `Node::is_focussable()`, the role from the tree `accessibility_tree` returns (a closed interactive list, so a disabled control is still held) and the listener mark `data-dioxus-id` (so a hidden control is still held, and so is an element whose listener a re-render removed, its mark still standing, so the check over-includes, conservative, while a `mounted` listener writes none — read, not run), with no second role mapping

**sr-actionable-keys starting reading ↔ the scope's re-pin**: the plan's pinned count reads Cells 677, the 676 data cells and `cells-grid`, elements that react to input, while the probe measures 676 reacting to `click` and `cells-grid` to `keydown` only; the re-pin of `stand_non_lean_tasks` must state which reading the field carries, so a click-only field reading `cells-grid` false keeps its role untouched (a11y-plan/screen-reader-support fct-pfylw46r) (a11y-plan/screen-reader-support fct-7vfy7k5v) (a11y-plan/screen-reader-support fct-pofw2owv)

**sr-author-id ↔ visual-visibility ↔ sr-tree bounds**: the graph's nodes must be exactly the snapshot's agent-visible tree nodes, keyed by `author_id`, with no hidden or inert node and with each node's bounds as the snapshot builds them; whether `TextRun` nodes, which carry no `author_id`, are graph nodes is a fork the plan must settle (a11y-plan/screen-reader-support fct-kf4qrij2) (a11y-plan/visual-design-verification fct-lq4s5uty) (a11y-plan/screen-reader-support fct-vee7m5at) (a11y-plan/screen-reader-support fct-jn5hbj7a)

**sr-snapshot masking ↔ the scope's never-logged rule**: a value the graph carries must read `MASKED_VALUE` as on every carrier, and neither the graph's read nor any log site may open a new exit for a value or an option's label (a11y-plan/screen-reader-support fct-ge4n5uhw) (a11y-plan/screen-reader-support fct-ljepgzwi)

body:
Builds the UI graph: one read that gives, for the current screen of a held instance, each node, the component that rendered it, its handlers, the state they write and the nodes that read that state (v030-05).
Link 1 and link 2 come from the dioxus-core vdom walk the stable ids already run (dynamic attributes, exact, `mounted` included); links 3 and 4 come from an escher-side signal registry in dioxus-native-dom that the stand's signals move onto.
Adds the «reacts to a click» reading as a closed boolean snapshot field, which absorbs residual res-gvelrxja and moves NODE_FIELDS (thirteen today), the schema help texts, describe() and every pin that counts them.
Keys the graph on the agent-visible accesskit node with an optional owner element, reserves a virtual-node id form that collides with none of the four current id forms, and lets a handler on an owner serve sub-targets.
Values stay masked and are never logged. The read crosses escher-driver's carriers as a new verb, outcome and MCP tool.

The snapshot model and its node fields: the new «reacts to a click» boolean joins NODE_FIELDS, the snapshot text form, parts, diff, MCP results and node-key help, and comes from the same snapshot model with no second role or name mapping.

The actionable-key rule and `DioxusDocument::unkeyed_actionable`: the plan says no snapshot field reports that an element reacts to a click and that the field is owed to «The UI graph». This chunk fulfils that, and the over-inclusive listener mark (a removed listener still counted) stays in force.

Stable element ids as AccessKit `author_id` on every element node of a Dioxus document: the graph is keyed on the agent-visible accesskit node as the snapshot is built, and link 1 reads through the same vdom walk.
Author key and id forms: the reserved virtual-node id form must collide with none of today's author key, anchored path, component path or document path, so actionable-key ids stay stable.
Role derivation: an element that reacts to a click and states no role reads GenericContainer. The new field must say it reacts, and the role must stay untouched.
Password and file input masking: a value the graph carries for state or a control reads `MASKED_VALUE`, the same as on every other carrier, and typed text appears in no field.
The obs log allowlist and redaction for escher_* and blitz* targets: no log site, span field or print may carry a node, a component name, a handler, a state or a value from the graph.
The stand's starting reading pinned by stand_non_lean_tasks (0 on the four lean tasks, Home, Temperature Converter, Circle Drawer 1, Cells 676), in both layout modes, re-pinned for the new field.

Snapshot diff carriers: the closed boolean sits inside the ratified snapshot and diff carriers and is no boundary widening under the 2026-10-10 rule. A new open value set on a carrier is a widening and the founder's fork.
Node bounds in the snapshot (client rects, an open list's row bounds): the graph's agent-visible node carries its bounds the way the snapshot builds them.
The accessibility tree build path through `Document::accessibility_tree` (DioxusDocument's override with stable ids): the graph reads the same tree nodes the snapshot consumes.
The seven_guis stand tasks whose hook-local signals move onto the registry: their stated roles, names and Tab orders in the shared tables must stay as they are.

body_fields.convention: A new accessibility or stand test file is listed in the a11y leg's file list, and a stand test that can flake is also named in the stand-repeat leg's three-round list.
A stand check asserts in both layout modes, from stated tables with their row counts asserted, and reads roles and names only from the shared module's tables.
A check of tree-derived readings reads them off the built tree after resolve, the snapshot model being the only consumer, never the element.

body: Colour contrast, the `stand_contrast` tables, `Harness::text_contrast` and the visual lint's contrast reading. The graph reads no colour.
Keyboard handling for range inputs, selects and listboxes, the CRUD list keys and Cells' arrows and editor. The chunk changes no key behaviour.
Focus order, focusability, the inert focus fixup and the disabled-ness keying. The chunk changes no focus rule.
The ARIA state attribute mapping (aria-selected, aria-pressed, aria-checked, aria-invalid) and upstream's label, description, expanded, disabled and level reads.
The platform adapter, its creation-before-shown rule and the windowed AT witness owned by res-llkgqygv.
Hidden-content and inert exclusion rules and hit pass-through.
The select list's painted colours and its motion, focus ring, colour scheme and user preferences.
Language and direction, text alternatives in fixtures, IME and cognitive error recovery cues.
Cells grid role and cell semantics (res-wvatzhpe) and the unread aria-activedescendant on the CRUD list.
Double click timing, pointer focus on click and the range input's pointer value setting.

body: **2026-10-06-accessibility-tree-identity** — (name sources, carried stable id, Dioxus feature wiring) made every element node of a Dioxus document carry its stable id as AccessKit `author_id`, with no `TextRun`, root or `Window` node carrying one, and put the `accessibility_tree` override behind dioxus-native-dom's `accessibility` feature. This chunk keys the graph on that `author_id`-carrying node, has to decide whether `TextRun` nodes count as graph nodes, and must reserve a virtual-node id form that no current `author_id` can collide with.

**2026-10-06-snapshot-model** — (the snapshot consumes the accessibility tree) made `DioxusDocument::snapshot` take role, name and focus from `accessibility_tree` with no second role or name mapping, and gated it under the `accessibility` feature. This is the rule the new «reacts to a click» field and the graph's agent-visible node must sit inside.

**2026-10-06-id-stability-across-code-edits** — (the actionable-key rule and its check) set the founder's rule that every actionable element (focusable, interactive role or listener) reads an author key, with `DioxusDocument::unkeyed_actionable` as the check and no second role mapping. Its trap: never satisfy the check by adding a `tabindex` or a role, because that moves the pinned Tab order. Moving the stand's signals onto the registry must leave this check empty.

**2026-10-06-snapshot-state-fidelity** — (a falsy `hidden` no longer drops a node) made the snapshot read `enabled`, `checked` and `value` from the element, because the tree gives none of them, and made a password read `MASKED_VALUE`. This is the source of the masking rule that any control value the graph carries must follow.

**2026-10-06-compact-snapshot-serialization** — (the text form reads the model; a file input's value is masked) made `Snapshot::to_text` a reader of the model only, one line per node, and extended `MASKED_VALUE` to a file input with a non-empty `value`. The new field must surface in `to_text` as one more model field, and the graph must mask file inputs the same way.

**2026-10-07-change-tracking-and-diff** — (the diff reads the snapshot model) made `Snapshot::diff` one more reader of the model with no second mapping, and added it to the feature-gated items the crate doc names. The new closed boolean has to flow through `diff` and `differs` as a model field.

**2026-10-07-audit-corrections** — (the stand's role and name tables stated once) put the stand checks' expected tables once in `tests/blitz-tests/tests/common/mod.rs`, as stated expectation and never a second mapping. The «reacts to a click» expectation rows this chunk re-pins should follow that shared-module pattern.

**2026-10-07-sink-target-allowlist** — (the obs sink described with its drop) recorded the target allowlist: safe fields only for `blitz*`/`accesskit_xplat`, `text`/`value`/`html`/`attrs` redacted for `escher_*`, any other target dropped whole. The scope's "never logged" rule for nodes, components, handlers, states and values binds to this allowlist, which names none of the graph's new content.

**2026-10-07-command-and-refusal-schema** — (the driver's `disabled` cause stated on the presence reading) set the rule that whatever detects `disabled` reads the snapshot's `enabled`, never the attribute's value, and that the driver's schema defines no role or name set of its own. How the new field reads a disabled control must agree with that.

**2026-10-07-refusal-detection** — (the `disabled` cause is detected) made `Session::run` refuse a `click` when `enabled` is `Some(false)`, read from the snapshot alone. Precedent: a disabled control's click is stopped, so the «reacts to a click» field must not call it reacting by some second disabled reading.

**2026-10-07-act-by-id** — (the session library names `accessibility`) has `escher-driver` name `accessibility` unconditionally, so the feature reaches seven_guis through that edge while its own manifest names none, and neither stand binary builds a platform adapter. The graph reader, the registry and the field must reach the stand through this edge, with no adapter joining.

**2026-10-10-snapshot-states** — (the tree states selected, toggled and invalid, and the snapshot takes them from it) grew `NodeState` to seven fields taken from the tree, never the element, each with a text token in a fixed order. This is the precedent for adding a closed field to the model, which this chunk does by moving `NODE_FIELDS` from thirteen to fourteen.

**2026-10-10-snapshot-states** — (the stand states a listbox, two toggle buttons and two invalid inputs) gave the CRUD list `role="listbox"`, rows `role="option"` with `aria-selected`, and the date inputs `aria-invalid`, by attribute alone with no element, class, style, key, id or order moving. The registry move must leave these attribute-stated roles and states exactly as they are.

**2026-10-10-mcp-surface** — (MCP results read the snapshot model) made an MCP tool result a further reader of the model only, with a `snapshot` block equal to `to_text` byte for byte. The new field reaches MCP results only through the model, and any new graph verb's MCP tool must not add a second mapping.

**2026-10-12-self-description** — (the password over MCP measured; the node keys' help and `differs` as readers) added the node keys' help (`help`) and `DiffNode::differs` as closed-word readers of the model, and measured a password reading `MASKED_VALUE` through MCP. The new field's help text and its `differs` name join these readers, and the scope says the schema's help texts and `describe()` move with it.

**2026-10-12-headless-screenshot** — (a password painted masked; the shot one more reader of bounds) left a password's typed text in no painted frame either, and made `screenshot` a reader of the model's bounds only. The graph's node bounds must match the snapshot's, and no carrier may expose a typed password.

**2026-10-13-stand-keyboard-harness** — (Enter and Space activate a focused control, and a click focuses a button) made a pointer click on a `button` or a submit/reset/button `input` focus it and end the walk, in every document, while any other click still clears focus. The field has to settle whether a native button's own activation, with no app handler, counts as reacting to a click.

**2026-10-13-stand-keyboard-harness** — (`disabled` by presence, the CRUD list's keys and the keyboard check) keyed disabled-ness one way, by presence, gave `crud-list` `tabindex="0"` and its Arrow/Home/End `onkeydown`, and added `stand_keyboard`. The CRUD list's `onkeydown` is the `keydown`-only handler the field has to classify, and its keys must keep acting after its signals move onto the registry.

**2026-10-14-stand-a11y-assertions** — (the enabled-state walks, the list named) asserted the walk against `ENABLED_TAB_ORDER` and named the list `People`; every interactive-role node of the lean tasks is named. The stand's stated Tab orders and names must hold after the registry move, with nothing re-baselined.

**2026-10-14-stand-requirement-sweep** — (every stand task keyed; the click-without-role count) made `unkeyed_actionable()` read 0 on the non-lean tasks too, and counted and pinned the elements that react to a click and state no role: 0 on the lean four, Home and Temperature Converter, Circle Drawer 1, Cells 676. No snapshot field said so, deferred on the founder's C3 «Замерить сейчас, поле позже (Рекомендую)». This is the starting reading the new field absorbs (residual `res-gvelrxja`), and where the scope's "Cells 676" comes from.

**2026-10-14-quality-gates** — (the stand's a11y files also run in `stand-repeat`) put every `stand_*` file into `stand-repeat`, three rounds under a zero-failure budget. The re-pinned `stand_non_lean_tasks` and `stand_actionable_keys` run there, so the new field's reading must be deterministic across rounds.

**2026-10-18-engine-debts** — (§5, §6: `inert` and `disabled` in focus order, keys and the hit) narrowed `disabled` to form controls (`ElementData::is_disabled`) for the pointer, click, activation and focus gates, and made a disabled form control stop the click walk while a disabled ancestor `div` does not. A node whose click the engine stops must never read as reacting.

**2026-10-18-engine-debts** — (the PROVISIONAL batch ratified by the founder) ratified the disabled-gate and click-walk marks (the founder, 2026-10-18). The disabled gate the field must agree with is ratified, not provisional.

**2026-10-20-large-screen-in-parts** — (the snapshot's parts, one more reader of the model) added `Snapshot::text_parts` as a reader of the model, so the crate doc names five feature-gated readers. The new field must read the same in every part, and the crate doc must name what the feature now also gates (the graph reader).

**2026-10-24-a11y-re-read** — (the a11y leg runs fourteen files) fixed the `a11y` leg at fourteen named files, on the founder's word. A test file this chunk adds to that leg would move the count, which is published in `docs/capabilities.md` and the CI pins.

**2026-10-25-capability-statement** — (the published accessibility reach) made `docs/capabilities.md` publish the reach (tier 0, three SC, the leg's fourteen files, named limits), with a pin that reads none of these claims. A change to the reach or the leg must be made in that document by hand.

**2026-10-25-cold-agent-bar** — (the flight booker's select in the stand's tables) replaced the mode buttons with `select#flight-type`, re-pinned `tab_order` and `ENABLED_TAB_ORDER`, and recorded that a driver `click` on a closed select's option is refused `covered`. The field must classify the closed select's options as taking no click.

**2026-10-25-cold-agent-bar** — (the served pages) brought Cells and the load page in as served pages beside the lean four, with `unkeyed_actionable` empty on all six served tasks. The registry move must keep all six keyed and the check empty.

**2026-10-31-engine-debts** — (the load page's and Cells' Tab, keyboard and contrast rows) added `LOAD_TAB_ORDER` and `CELLS_TAB_ORDER` in the shared module, walked by `stand_keyboard`, with keyboard and contrast rows for `load-fetch` and `cells-grid`. These are the stated sequences that must hold after Cells' and the load page's signals move onto the registry.

**2026-10-31-engine-debts** — (Cells by keyboard) made `cells-grid` (aria-label `Cells`, no role) one Tab stop with an `onkeydown`, its arrows moving `current` through a synchronous `MountedData::scroll_to`. It re-said the reacting-elements reading from «react to a click, Cells 676» to «react to input, Cells 677», disproving the plan's forecast. This is the 676-vs-677 discrepancy the field's re-pin must resolve, and the place where `keydown`-only must be decided explicitly. Role and cell semantics stay out by residual.

**2026-10-31-engine-debts** — (a `multiple` select's keys and row clicks) added `click_select_row` behind `handle_click`'s `option` arm: a disabled select stops it and a disabled row changes nothing, and an option of a closed single select is not clicked. The field must read these rows the way the click path treats them.

**2026-10-31-engine-debts** — (the `MountedData` hazard in a spawned task) first recorded the `RefCell already borrowed` panic from a key handler's spawned task, which is why Cells calls its handles synchronously. Background for registry writes inside key handlers.

**2026-10-31-select-popup** — (a single select's `expanded` in the tree) let a single select write `expanded` from its list's open state, read as a closed bool of engine state inside the states class and outside the widening. Precedent for the scope's claim that a closed boolean field is no boundary widening.

**2026-10-31-select-popup** — (what opens a single select's list; a click, the pointer and focus on an open list) made a click on a single select open or close its list while a disabled, inert, hidden or empty select opens nothing, and let an open list's row take a click behind `click_lands_on_row`. The field must agree with these click paths.

**2026-10-31-select-popup** — (what the snapshot and an assistive technology read of an open list) left no `expanded` node key, so `NODE_FIELDS` reads thirteen (the field rule of 2026-10-10, on the operator's call), and made an open row's `bounds` its painted row's. This is the count this chunk moves to fourteen and the bounds rule the graph's nodes follow.

**2026-10-31-select-popup** — (how an open list's labels leave) ratified that option and group labels leave only as painted pixels and the snapshot's `name`, with no log site. The graph's read and its log sites must open no new exit for them.

**2026-11-04-dioxus-runtime-probe** — (the «reacts to a click» reading measured by link 2) re-owned the reading from a residual to a measured reading whose snapshot field is owed to «The UI graph»: Cells 677 = 676 `click` + `cells-grid` `keydown`; Counter `counter-increment` `click`, `counter-value` none; CRUD `crud-list` `keydown`; `NODE_FIELDS` thirteen. This is the measured basis the field must agree with, while the C3 ruling and the count as starting point stand.

**2026-11-04-dioxus-runtime-probe** — (the listener mark's over-report and the actionable-key check) recorded that `data-dioxus-id` over-includes an element whose listener a re-render removed and that a `mounted` listener writes none, while the vdom walk's dynamic attributes (`VNode.dynamic_attrs`, `VNode::mounted_dynamic_attribute`) read listeners exactly. So link 2 and the field read the vdom walk, `unkeyed_actionable` keeps the mark, and the two readings may differ.

**2026-11-04-dioxus-runtime-probe** — (the probe target outside the a11y leg) placed `dioxus_runtime_probe` (10 tests, both modes) in none of the a11y leg's fourteen files and outside `stand-repeat`, reached by the workspace `test` leg. Its link-2 pins move with the field but leave the leg unmoved.

**2026-11-04-dioxus-runtime-probe** — (the MountedData hazard re-measured, its fix routed) found that `DioxusDocument::poll` holds `inner.borrow_mut()` across `render_immediate` (two `should_panic` pins) and routed the fix to «MountedData buffered render». History behind the borrow discipline the registry's write and the `VirtualDom::in_runtime` graph read must respect.

**2026-11-05-residuals-repoint** — re-pointed the plan's owner sentences from `.andromeda/residuals.md` to residual rows (`res-wvatzhpe` among them). An owner this chunk retires or absorbs, such as `res-gvelrxja`, is named by its residual row, not by the retired file.

**2026-11-07-mounteddata-buffered-render** — (the residual owner clauses re-said to their rows' status) gave `res-wvatzhpe` (Cells' role and cell semantics kept out) «re-carried at 0.3.0 (target: next)». The field must say `cells-grid` reacts while its role stays out under that residual, and any owner clause this chunk touches must carry its row's status.

**2026-11-07-mounteddata-buffered-render** — (citations re-pointed to the bridge's and the probe's moved lines) re-pointed citations into `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/dioxus_document.rs` (`accessibility_tree` override 324-340), `lib.rs` (feature range 23-28) and `tests/blitz-tests/tests/dioxus_runtime_probe.rs` (link 2 at 281-316 and 339-367, over-report 386-428). This chunk edits these same files, so these citations move again.

**2026-11-07-mounteddata-buffered-render** — (the spawned-task MountedData hazard record, closed by the buffered render) made `initial_build` and `Document::poll` render into `buffered_mutations` with the document unborrowed, then replay once through one `MutationWriter`, witnessed by two probe pins in both modes; Cells' synchronous calls were kept. The registry's wrapper write in key handlers and spawned tasks must take no document borrow of its own and keep these pins green.

**2026-11-07-mounteddata-buffered-render** — (the buffered render's same-render limit) recorded that a task polled during a render sees the document as the previous render left it, so a node created in the same render is absent; owned by an open residual (target: next). Any graph or registry read inside a render meets this limit.

partial — no new UI surface, focus, keys or contrast; the chunk turns on the snapshot model and the actionable-key rule (§7), which the plan names as owing the «reacts to a click» field to this entry.

- a11y-plan §7 Screen Reader Support (sr-snapshot) requires the snapshot to take role, name, focus and states from `accessibility_tree`, never the element, and its text form, parts, diff, MCP results and node-key help to read that model alone, never a second role or name mapping; the graph keyed on the agent-visible node, and the new «reacts to a click» field, must sit inside that rule.
- a11y-plan §7 Screen Reader Support (sr-actionable-keys) requires every element an agent can act on to read an author key with `DioxusDocument::unkeyed_actionable` as the check, no second role mapping; it says no snapshot field reports that an element reacts to a click, a reading measured by link 2 and owed as a field to the route entry «The UI graph» (founder's C3, 2026-10-14). The new field is how this chunk meets that owed reading.
- a11y-plan §7 Screen Reader Support (sr-actionable-keys) records the starting count of elements that react to input and state no interactive role (`stand_non_lean_tasks`) as 0 on the four lean tasks, Home and Temperature Converter, Circle Drawer 1, Cells 677 (676 data cells plus `cells-grid`). The scope says "Cells 676". Which number is right is research's question, and the pin the field moves must match the measured one.
- a11y-plan §7 Screen Reader Support (sr-actionable-keys) states that the listener mark over-includes (a listener removed on re-render keeps its mark) and that a `mounted` listener writes no mark; per the same section, the probe's link 2 reading (Cells 677 = 676 `click` + `cells-grid` `keydown`; Counter `counter-increment` `click`; CRUD `crud-list` `keydown`) is the measured basis the field's reading must agree with.
- a11y-plan §7 Screen Reader Support (sr-tree) requires each element node of a Dioxus document to carry its stable element id as AccessKit `author_id` (no TextRun, root or Window node carries one). A reserved virtual-node id form must not collide with the author ids the tree carries, and whether today's ids already exclude the separator is research's question.
- a11y-plan §7 Screen Reader Support (sr-snapshot) requires a password's value to read as `MASKED_VALUE` (a file input with a value reads the same marker) and its typed text to appear in no snapshot field or tree node; a control value the graph carries must read the same.

- Snapshot fields derive from the built tree through `DioxusDocument::snapshot`. The new closed boolean field goes in beside the existing thirteen `NODE_FIELDS` (per a11y-plan §7 Screen Reader Support).
- `unkeyed_actionable` reads the listener mark `data-dioxus-id` together with focusability and the tree's role. The graph's link 2 should read the vdom's dynamic attributes instead (exact, `mounted` included), so the two readings differ where the mark over-includes (per a11y-plan §7 Screen Reader Support).
- Stand checks state their expected tables once in a shared module and assert row counts in both layout modes (per a11y-plan §3 A11y Assertion Harness Contract; a11y-plan §7 Screen Reader Support).

- No second role or name mapping. The graph and the «reacts to a click» field must not derive role or name from the element instead of the tree (per a11y-plan §7 Screen Reader Support).
- An unmasked password or file-input value must not appear in any graph output or snapshot field (per a11y-plan §7 Screen Reader Support).

- a11y ↔ tests: the `stand_non_lean_tasks` count, `stand_actionable_keys` and `dioxus_runtime_probe` pins move with `NODE_FIELDS`. `dioxus_runtime_probe` is none of the `a11y` leg's fourteen files (per a11y-plan §9 CI Integration).
- a11y ↔ obs/security: the masking rule (§7) binds to the scope's "never logged" rule (obs plan §6 allowlist).

- On every stand task, in both layout modes, the «reacts to a click» snapshot field agrees with the measured link 2 reading: Cells' 676 data cells for `click`, `counter-increment` true and `counter-value` false. Whether `keydown` alone counts (`cells-grid`, `crud-list`) is stated explicitly and pinned (per a11y-plan §7 Screen Reader Support).
- `unkeyed_actionable` still returns nothing on every stand task after the stand's signals move onto the registry (per a11y-plan §7 Screen Reader Support).
- The snapshot's role and name still equal the tree's, node for node, with the new field added and no second mapping (per a11y-plan §7 Screen Reader Support).
- No graph or snapshot output carries a password's or file input's typed value. Each reads `MASKED_VALUE` (per a11y-plan §7 Screen Reader Support).

body:
Builds the UI graph (v030-05): one read that gives, for the current screen of a held instance, each node, the component that rendered it, its handlers, the state those handlers write and the nodes that read that state.
Link 1 and link 2 are read by the public dioxus-core vdom walk the stable ids already run, link 2 through the dynamic attributes (exact, `mounted` included); links 3 and 4 come through a new escher-side signal registry in dioxus-native-dom, and the seven_guis stand's signals move onto it.
Adds the «reacts to a click» reading as a closed boolean snapshot field, which absorbs residual res-gvelrxja and moves `NODE_FIELDS` (thirteen today), the schema help texts, `describe()` and every pin that counts them; values stay masked and nothing is logged.
Carries the canvas direction: reserve a virtual-node id form that collides with none of the four stable-id tiers, key the graph on the agent-visible accesskit node with an optional owner element, and let a handler on an owner serve sub-targets. A contract or boundary change from this is the founder's fork, asked at P4.
The read crosses the driver's carriers (a verb, an outcome, its written form, its MCP tool, its recorded step). Expected crates: dioxus-native-dom, escher-driver, seven_guis. No blitz-dom engine change is expected.

The Dioxus DOM bridge's stable ids: `DioxusDocument::element_id` / `element_ids` and their four tiers (author key, anchored path, component path, document path). The graph's link 1 reuses their vdom walk. The reserved virtual-node id form must use a separator that no id of the four tiers can hold.

`DioxusDocument::unkeyed_actionable` and the rule that every actionable element reads an author key: it detects an id that holds a `/`, so the reserved virtual-node separator must not change what it reports.

The snapshot, its text form and its diff under `accessibility`: they read the screen read-only and hold no `NodeId`. The new «reacts to a click» closed boolean joins the node's fields, and `NODE_FIELDS`, the schema help texts, `describe()` and every count pin move with it. Under the 2026-10-10 rule this is no widening.

`build_accessibility_tree` and its AccessKit `TreeUpdate`, which builds the agent-visible nodes and their bounds. The graph is keyed on that node with an optional owner element, never on a DOM `NodeId`.

The Dioxus integration on Dioxus 0.7.3 (dioxus-core 0.7.10), with no fork and no engine change. The registry reads link 4 through `Readable::subscribers()` inside `VirtualDom::in_runtime` and each subscriber's `ReactiveContext::origin_scope()`. A scope's hooks are `pub(crate)`, so a signal is found only through the wrapper hook or context an app hands it to.

DOM events reach the vdom through `data-dioxus-id`, and Dioxus skips event kinds with zero handlers. Link 2 reads handlers from `VNode.dynamic_attrs` / `VNode::mounted_dynamic_attribute`, not from the attributes, which over-report. A handler on an owner element may serve sub-targets.

The driver session's command schema: `VERBS` (twelve verbs), the eight closed causes, `Session::run` validating first, and nothing public running a `Command` that did not come from `validate`. A new verb and outcome for the graph read must join that `'static` schema and its count pins.

The driver's carriers: the `v3` wire, the `escher-session` command line and its usage table, the MCP server and its tools, and the `command` and `tool_call` spans. Each answer is written by hand in the crate-private `json` module, no serialization crate writes one, and no ending writes back what the caller typed.

The boundary rule (security rules §Surfaces, the rule of 2026-10-10): a new carrier or exit, or a new open value set on a ratified carrier, widens the boundary and is the founder's fork. Component names, handler event names and registered state names going out are such a question.

Masking: `is_masked_input` (a password or file input) is the one masked-control test, and `MASKED_VALUE` stands in for its value. Every state or control value the graph carries reads masked as on every carrier.

No log or event carries the snapshot, its text or a diff, except a diff's three counts on the command span. No log site, span field or print may carry a node, a component name, a handler, a state or a value. escher-driver builds its spans by hand, logs no id, name or value and installs no subscriber.
escher-telemetry's scrubbing (`SAFE_FIELDS`, `CONTENT_FIELDS` always redacted, targets outside the prefix sets dropped) stands behind the never-logged rule. The graph adds no field it must print.

The headless stand (`seven_guis::stand`): the four lean tasks, Cells (`boot_cells`) and the load page, in a pinned 800x600 Light viewport. The stand's hook-local signals move onto the registry. It installs no telemetry and reads no env var. `stand_non_lean_tasks` pins the starting «reacts to a click» reading on the four lean tasks, Cells and both layout modes.

The recording and kept checks: the graph read's recorded step, `Check::replay` running through `Session::run`, a masked value's stand-in, and the two committed kept checks under `tests/blitz-tests/checks/` that `stand_replay` replays.

The served stand tasks of the `escher-session` command line and the MCP `start` tool's `enum`, both written from one private table. The capability statement (`docs/capabilities.md`) and the root `README.md` give the count of driver commands an MCP client gets as tools, and a pin reads that count.

Config management and feature gating: the `accessibility` feature gates the dioxus-native-dom snapshot modules. The graph reader and the snapshot field follow that gating, and features are forwarded down the crates.
Apps and examples conventions for the stand: reactive state through `#[derive(Store)]` and signal and store hooks. The stand's signals, wrapped by the registry, keep those hooks' behaviour.

Manifests: a dependency the registry or graph reader takes (for example dioxus-core) is declared once in `[workspace.dependencies]`, used as `{ workspace = true }`, and in-repo crates take `default-features = false`.

Visibility and naming: crate internals stay `pub(crate)` / `pub(super)`. Builder methods follow `with_…` / `without_…`. Every public item of the registry and graph reader carries rustdoc, under the workflow-wide `-D warnings`.
The direct engine changes for every document and their merge surfaces: the chunk adds none (no blitz-dom change is expected), so that list and the Upstream sync line it owns must stay as they are.

body_fields.convention: Each new test sits in a `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` at the end of its source file or in a `#[path]` child file. Each integration test file covers one behaviour and opens with a `//!` doc naming it. Scenarios run in both layout modes, tests first assert that the fixture produces the condition, and stand checks share helpers through non-target modules under `tests/`.
Each new module or file opens with a `//!` doc. Public items carry `///`, and constants state their rationale.

Each change passes `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --locked -- -D warnings` and rustdoc `-D warnings` through `.github/scripts/ci-leg.sh` legs. `expect` / `unwrap` carry a justification.
Tracing in the engine crates is gated per call site with a `cfg(not(feature = "tracing"))` fallback. escher's own crates take `tracing` ungated, with spans built by hand and no `#[instrument]`.
Error types are enums with `Display` and a `From` per wrapped error. Mutex locks recover from poisoning with `into_inner`.
The per-crate coverage floor and the `stand-repeat` leg's zero-failure budget hold for each new crate code and stand check.

body: The browser app (history store, URL suggester, about pages, document loader) and rdme: the graph is read on the headless stand and the driver, not in those apps.
The WPT runner, its outputs, bucketing and execution model: the chunk adds no WPT test and changes no runner.
Networking (blitz-net, the `User-Agent`, the per-host semaphore, the HTTP cache) and resource loading: the graph makes no fetch.
Paint and shell (blitz-paint, layer caps, renderer backends, blitz-shell's loop and windowing, keyboard shortcuts): the graph is a read and paints nothing. The canvas renderer is out of scope.
JavaScript on Boa (blitz-vibey-script, timers, the module loader, `document_may_load`): the stand is a Dioxus app, so no script is involved.
Layout, CSS approximations, unsupported features, fonts, inline SVG and HTML parsing decisions: the graph reads already-built nodes and changes no style or layout.
Deployment, Nix packaging, cross-compilation, publish-browser bundles and signed builds: the chunk adds no build target or package.
Licensing exceptions and the HTML fixture conventions under `examples/assets`: the chunk adds no licensed asset and no HTML fixture page.
The stylo threading lock, the thread-local layout context, mimalloc and the WPT panic hook: the graph read spawns no thread and touches no process-wide engine state.
«What can I do here» (v030-06), «Handler coverage» (v030-07), virtual-node production, `drag` and the canvas renderer are out of scope. Only the id form is reserved; nothing produces it.

body: **2026-10-06-stable-element-ids** — registered `DioxusDocument::element_id` / `element_ids`, computed on demand from a vdom walk joined with a DOM walk and written to neither DOM nor vdom. The grammar: author key `/`-free; component path segments are the last `::` segment of `VComponent.name` with generics stripped, with dioxus-core's four framework scopes adding none; document path `/{tag}:{n}…`; no `NodeId`, `ElementId`, `ScopeId` or pointer in an id. The plan's assumptions (the base scope is `root`, `VComponent.name` is a bare name) were corrected by measurement. This is the grammar the reserved virtual-node separator must not collide with, and the walk that link 1 reuses and that names components.

**2026-10-06-id-stability-across-code-edits** — added the fourth tier, the anchored path `{key}//{segment}` (the only id holding `//`, acting inside one component only), and registered `unkeyed_actionable` (focusable · interactive role · `data-dioxus-id`). The founder ruled out a bare `key/segment` and a leading `#`. Trap it set: `UnkeyedActionable.node` is a process-local `NodeId`, so no wire form may carry it. Two rules follow for this chunk. The virtual-node separator must avoid `/`, `//` and the spellings the founder rejected, and must leave the `/` test unchanged. The graph must apply the same no-`NodeId` rule to `Target.node`.

**2026-10-06-accessibility-tree-identity** — the `Document::accessibility_tree` default, with `DioxusDocument` alone overriding it to set each element node's AccessKit `author_id` to its stable id (none on `TextRun`, root or `Window`). dioxus-native-dom's `accessibility` = `["blitz-dom/accessibility", "dep:accesskit"]`; seven_guis does not name it. This is the agent-visible node the graph keys on. Trap recorded: a feature-gated item can pass under `cargo test --workspace` and be compiled out under `-p blitz-tests` (check `cargo tree -e features -i`). That matters for the `accessibility`-gated graph reader and for a seven_guis registry reached without that feature.

**2026-10-06-snapshot-model** — registered `DioxusDocument::snapshot` under `accessibility`: `SnapshotNode { id, role, name, state, bounds, children }`, where a node is every element the accessibility tree keeps, resolved through `get_node`, and no field holds a `NodeId`, tree id, `ElementId`, `ScopeId` or pointer. Standing rule: the snapshot derives no role or name of its own, so it cannot disagree with the tree. The «reacts to a click» field joins this model, and the graph keyed on the same node inherits the no-`NodeId` and no-second-derivation rules.

**2026-10-06-snapshot-state-fidelity** — the password `value` reads `MASKED_VALUE` (one fixed marker, the operator's answer), never the text or its length. Weighed and ruled out: a fifth `NodeState` field or a changed `value` type to mark a masked value. Precedent for this chunk on two counts. Masking of any value the graph carries goes through this one form. Adding a `NodeState` field has been weighed against the model before.

**2026-10-06-compact-snapshot-serialization** — `Snapshot::to_text`: fixed state-token order, `SNAPSHOT_TEXT_BUDGET` 10,000, the lean screens' sizes measured. The mask was extended to a file `input`. Standing rule: each later surface asks again when the text first leaves the process. A «reacts to a click» token, if the text form carries one, moves this token order and the pinned lean-task sizes.

**2026-10-07-change-tracking-and-diff** — `Snapshot::diff` → `SnapshotDiff { added, removed, changed }`, not derived from the engine-touched changed set (a superset of snapshot-changed). The click field's diff reading must come from the snapshots, not from the changed set.

**2026-10-07-command-and-refusal-schema** — the one `'static` schema (`VERBS`, `VerbSpec`/`ArgSpec`/`FieldSpec`, `validate`, `Cause` closed at eight, `Fault`, none holding a `String`). Rules set for later chunks: a later entry adds its verbs to `VERBS`, never a second table; `Command`, `Call` and `ArgValue` print ids and typed text under `Debug`, so nothing fields them. The graph verb follows this path.

**2026-10-07-act-by-id** — `Session::run` is the one entry point: `validate` first, and nothing public runs a `Command` that did not come from `validate`. Nothing resolved (no id, no `NodeId`) outlives a call, and nothing fields an `Outcome`, whose `Debug` prints ids, names and values. Standing rule: the first command carrying a call or an outcome out of the process is a crossing question. A graph `Outcome` falls under these rules. The graph must not let a `NodeId` outlive a call on the session.

**2026-10-07-refusal-detection** — a sixth verb (`scroll`), ratified by the founder as a widening, with `Command::Scroll` and `Outcome::Scrolled`. The session's record of ids, `SeenIds` (`MAX_SEEN_IDS` 4096), is fed from snapshots, and `stale` vs `not-found` is decided from it. Rule restated: a verb joins `VERBS`, never a second table. Two consequences here: a new verb has been a founder's widening every time, and whether a graph read feeds the record of ids must be decided.

**2026-10-07-driver-command-spans** — the `command` span (target `escher_driver`, INFO, `info_span!`, no `#[instrument]`) with its eight fields. `snapshot` records `verb` alone. relevant

- Stable ids: architecture §Standard Contracts → Dioxus DOM bridge requires `DioxusDocument::element_id` / `element_ids` to compute ids on demand in four tiers (author key, anchored path, component path, document path), written to neither the DOM nor the vdom. The reserved virtual-node form (`{canvas element}` + `{virtual key}`) must use a separator none of those four tiers can produce. Whether today's id grammar leaves such a separator free is research's question.
- No `NodeId` crosses: architecture §Standard Contracts → Dioxus DOM bridge requires the snapshot, its text form and its diff to read the screen read-only and hold no `NodeId`. A graph keyed on the agent-visible node with an optional owner element must keep `NodeId` (`Target.node`) inside the crate and never let it reach a carrier.
- Driver schema: architecture §Standard Contracts → Driver session requires the command and refusal schema to be stated once as `'static` data (twelve verbs, eight closed causes, no refusal holding what a call supplied). It also requires every call to go through `Session::run`, which validates first, and every answer to be written by hand in the crate-private `json` module. A new graph verb or outcome changes that stated schema, so it is the founder's fork.
- Carrier boundary: architecture §Established Decisions → Driver session says ids, names, masked values, snapshot text, diffs, shots and lint findings cross, and never a `NodeId`. It also says a new carrier or exit widens the boundary. Component names, handler event names and registered state names going out on the `v3` wire or over MCP are new content on a ratified carrier, so that content set goes to the founder at P4.
- Identity safety: architecture §Design Philosophy requires versioned node ids, public APIs that take `NodeId`, and persistent interaction state that references DOM nodes only. The owner-element link and any graph state held across reads must follow this rule, and must not key persistent state on accesskit or layout-generated nodes.
- Masking: architecture §Standard Contracts → Dioxus DOM bridge makes `is_masked_input` the one masked-control test (a password or file `input`). Any control value the graph carries must be masked through that one test, with no second masking rule.
- Gating and logging: architecture §Cross-cutting Patterns → Config management puts the `accessibility` feature as the gate on the dioxus-native-dom snapshot modules, which covers the new snapshot field and the graph reader that builds on the snapshot. Architecture §Conventions → Feature gating requires escher-driver's spans to be built by hand with no `#[instrument]`, so no graph content can enter a span field by accident.

- Read-only bridge readers on `DioxusDocument` that compute on demand and change nothing, for example `element_id`, `element_ids` and `unkeyed_actionable` with its remedy (architecture §Standard Contracts → Dioxus DOM bridge). The graph reader and the signal registry's reads follow the same shape.
- One validated path: `Session::run` validates first, nothing public runs a `Command` that did not come from `validate`, and the recording replays answered calls through `Check::replay` (architecture §Standard Contracts → Driver session). A graph read gets its verb, its recorded step and its MCP tool through this path.
- Manifests: dependencies are declared once in `[workspace.dependencies]`, in-repo crates use `default-features = false`, and optional capabilities are Cargo features forwarded across crates (architecture §Conventions → Manifests; architecture §Project Intent → Growth model). The registry stays inside dioxus-native-dom on Dioxus "0.7.3" with no fork (architecture §Inherited Defaults).
- Apps and examples: Dioxus examples use `#[component]` with signal and store hooks (architecture §Conventions → Apps and examples). Moving the seven_guis stand's signals onto the registry's wrapper hook keeps that shape.

- No serialization crate writes a driver answer. `serde_json` only reads MCP requests and kept checks, and no command's ending writes back anything the caller typed (architecture §Standard Contracts → Driver session).
- No log, event or span carries the snapshot, its text or a diff, except a diff's three counts on the command span (architecture §Standard Contracts → Dioxus DOM bridge). This extends to graph nodes, component names, handlers, states and values.
- No new direct engine change for every document in blitz-dom without ratification. Architecture §Established Decisions lists each such change as ratified and flagged upstreamable, with a merge surface owned by Upstream sync. The scope expects none.

- arch ↔ security: adding a verb, an outcome or open-valued content (component, handler or state names) to the ratified `v3` / MCP carriers widens the boundary (architecture §Established Decisions → Driver session). The founder decides it at P4 under security §Surfaces.
- arch ↔ tests: the snapshot field changes `NODE_FIELDS` (thirteen), and a new verb changes the twelve-verb schema (architecture §Standard Contracts → Driver session). Every pin that counts either one, including the capability-statement pin of driver commands exposed as MCP tools (architecture §Project Intent → Front page), must move with the change. Stand scenarios run in both layout modes (architecture §Conventions → Tests).
- arch ↔ obs: escher-driver's ungated `command` / `tool_call` spans must carry no graph content (architecture §Conventions → Feature gating; architecture §Cross-cutting Patterns → Logging and timing).

- (arch) The new code lives in `dioxus-native-dom` (graph reader, signal registry, snapshot field), `escher-driver` (the read's carriers) and `seven_guis` (the stand's signals). blitz-dom gets no engine change, and no Dioxus fork or version change lands (per architecture §Inherited Defaults).
- (arch) No graph answer, snapshot field or recorded step holds a `NodeId`. Every answer is written in the crate-private `json` module through `Session::run` (per architecture §Standard Contracts → Driver session).
- (arch) The reserved virtual-node id form is shown not to collide with any of the four stable-id tiers, by a separator none of them can hold. Nothing in 0.3.0 produces such an id (per architecture §Standard Contracts → Dioxus DOM bridge).
- (arch) Any change to the verb count, the cause set or the carriers' content is handed to the founder as a fork, not landed by the plan (per architecture §Established Decisions → Driver session).

body:
Builds one read that gives, for the current screen of a held instance, each node, the component that rendered it, the handlers it carries, the state those handlers write and the nodes that read that state (v030-05).
Links 1 and 2 come from the dioxus-core vdom walk the stable ids already run; links 3 and 4 come from an escher-side signal registry in dioxus-native-dom that the seven_guis stand's signals move onto.
Adds a closed boolean snapshot field saying a node reacts to a click, which moves NODE_FIELDS (thirteen today), the schema help texts and describe(), and absorbs residual res-gvelrxja.
Masks values on every carrier, and logs no node, component, handler, state or value. Reserves a virtual-node id form, keys the graph on the agent-visible node with an optional owner element, and lets a handler on an owner serve sub-targets.

body_fields.what: the snapshot node's reacts-to-a-click field, values masked as MASKED_VALUE
NODE_FIELDS, the schema help texts, VERBS

body: The driver command line and its mcp role are agent surfaces: a new verb, its outcome, written form and MCP tool must print only JSON on stdout, one line per command or JSON-RPC 2.0 lines, never colour or an ESC byte, with no terminal test, and keep the exit status classes (0 accepted, 1 refused, 2 usage, 3 session error).
The cli surface component patterns for escher-session: the graph read's answer and its refusals cross this surface and follow its output rules.
The reacts-to-a-click reading: an element that reacts to a click and states no role reads GenericContainer today; the new boolean must say it reacts, inside the ratified snapshot and diff carriers.
Masked values: a password's or a file input's value, and any state or control value the graph carries, reads as MASKED_VALUE on every carrier.
The seven_guis stand tasks (Home, Temperature Converter, Circle Drawer, Cells) whose signals move onto the registry, and the starting reading pinned on the four lean tasks in both layout modes.

The graph is keyed on the agent-visible accesskit node with its bounds, as the snapshot is built, with an optional owner element; a canvas or custom-widget element whose one listener dispatches inside is the owner case.
The web-spa surface renders into one canvas: the reserved virtual-node id form (canvas element plus virtual key) is direction for it, with no canvas renderer or virtual-node production in this chunk.
The engine's cursor reading (Pointer inside links, Default otherwise) is not a reacts-to-a-click signal; the new field is read from the handlers the vdom walk finds, not from the cursor.

body_fields.convention: The driver's command line and mcp output carry only JSON on stdout with the exit status classes; any new verb, its test and its recorded step follow it.

body: Color palette, core colors, surface scale, text hierarchy, semantic colors and border progression: the chunk paints nothing and adds no colour.
The open select list's engine-painted colour constants: the chunk touches no select list painting.
Typography, font loading and the screenshot fonts-unavailable refusal: the graph read takes no screenshot and measures no text.
Spacing values and scales: the chunk changes no layout or spacing.
Border radius: the chunk changes no box shape.
Motion, the virtual clock, settle, advance and the load wait: the graph read moves no clock and drives no animation.
Iconography of the browser toolbar, IconButton, favicons and bundle icons: the chunk touches no browser app icon.
Desktop-native and mobile-native surface tokens, titlebar, url bar, back button, window and capture patterns: the chunk changes no shell or browser app surface.
Depth strategy elevation values and hit-testing clip rules: the graph read does no hit-testing.
