body: **2026-10-10-driver-cli** — (the driver command line's output form) set the `escher-session` stdout form: one line of JSON per command keyed by the driver schema's own words and nothing else on stdout, usage errors one fixed stderr line, no colour/colour dependency, no ESC byte, no terminal test, exit classes 0 accepted · 1 refused · 2 usage · 3 session error; the founder's answers of 2026-10-10. This is the form the new graph verb's CLI answer must take (the extract's first three constraints and its acceptance line).

**2026-10-10-mcp-surface** — (the `mcp` role's stdout) added the `mcp` role: newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0 lines only, a reply per non-notification request, a tool result's text the JSON line (screen text for `snapshot`), no ESC byte asserted on every reply by the shared `Speaker`, no-terminal-test search counting 0. The graph verb's MCP tool rests on this rule and passes through that same `Speaker` assertion.

**2026-10-12-self-description** — (`escher-session help` and the exit-status table) made the four exit classes read from the schema's `EXIT_STATUSES` table that `help` serves, and gave a `help` tool result's text as the self-description's line. The new verb must add no exit and stay in that table, and its addition to `VERBS` shows in `help`'s self-description.

**2026-10-12-headless-screenshot** — (the shot's answer line, the MCP image block) set `screenshot`'s answer as one uncoloured `{"width","height","png"}` line and its MCP reply as an `image` block then a text block, every reply still one line with no ESC byte; the founder's fork 1 (2026-10-12). This is the template the extract names for a new verb's written form and MCP tool, and the precedent that a new content shape on the carrier went to the founder.

**2026-10-20-large-screen-in-parts** — (the paged `snapshot` answer line) set `snapshot [--part]`'s line `{"text":…}` / `{"text":…,"part":n,"parts":m}` and changed its MCP result from screen text to the JSON line, ratified by the founder (F1). The other template for the graph verb's answer, and the precedent that a change to an answer shape on the cli carrier is the founder's fork; a large graph answer may meet the same paging question.

**2026-10-19-session-recording** — (the two recording session errors in the exit-3 class) put `record-dir-not-private` and `recording-failed` in the exit-3 class with no new exit, as fixed text inside a ratified carrier. Precedent for the graph verb's own refusals or session errors fitting the existing classes, and for its recorded step (scope's «its recorded step»).

**2026-10-25-cold-agent-bar** — (Cli item) `escher-session` serves six tasks (`counter` · `flight-booker` · `timer` · `crud` · `cells` · `load`), the usage line and the MCP `start` tool's `enum` listing them; it also added the overlay scrollbar's band behaviour for a Cells click. The graph read runs over these served stand tasks (the scope's `stand_non_lean_tasks` pins and its v030-05 acceptance), and the Cells click caveat stays when the stand's signals move onto the registry.

**2026-10-31-select-popup** — (what the tree, the snapshot and a shot read of an open list) the highlighted row is in no snapshot and no tree; a row of an open list carries its own `bounds` in the snapshot and a `screenshot` of a row crops to it, leaving the list open; the snapshot's builder reads the row's list bounds before its client rect; the answer card read the row's `bounds` as outside the boundary widening, a closed set inside the ratified crossing. This is fct-grd6lupt, the precedent for an agent-visible node with an optional owner the graph must key on, and the precedent for the «reacts to a click» boolean being no widening.

**2026-10-31-select-popup** — (the open select list answers the hit before the page's walk) a row of an open select list stands outside the page's hit walk, answered first by `select_list_hit` in `hit_with_scrollbar`, so a box clipping the select clips no row, and `hit`, `set_hover_to`, `handle_pointerdown` and the driver's `covered` all read it. The extract's constraint that a sub-target served by its owner must not change hit-testing rests on this entry.

**2026-10-31-select-popup** — (a single select's list is painted, an engine overlay) on desktop-native the list is an engine overlay reached through `paint_scene` alone, not a second OS window and not rows as boxes (`:open` plus rows as boxes stand rejected). The rows have no DOM element of their own, which is why the graph must key on the accesskit node with an owner element rather than on `Target.node`.

**2026-10-31-select-popup** — (how a single select's list opens, moves, chooses and closes) the list's open/choose/close behaviour, fired events (`input` then `change`) and the openers (a click, Enter, Space) are all handled by the select's own handler. This is the owner-served sub-target the scope's «a handler sits on an owner element and serves sub-targets» direction generalises; the graph's handlers for a row are the select's.

**2026-10-10-scrolling-box-bounds-and-hit** — (the hit walk's edge rule) the page's hit walk stops at the padding box of a node that clips by `overflow`. This is the clip rule the select list's rows stand outside of (n=9); keying the graph on owner-keyed nodes must leave it as it is.

**2026-10-18-engine-debts** — (the hit stops at a `contain: paint` box) widened the stop to a box paint clips by `overflow` or computed `contain: paint`, later ratified by the founder. Part of the same hit rule the owner-served sub-targets must not change.

**2026-10-18-upstream-sync-determinism-and-traces** — (§Iconography: the cursor over no box reads Default) «Default otherwise» now covers a pointer over no box; with the 2026-10-18 ratification this is the cursor reading of fct-guxvotwt. The cascade binds that the «reacts to a click» field is read from handlers, never from this cursor reading.

**2026-10-07-act-by-id** — (the driver's `advance` moves app time) `advance` moves an app's own time through the step a session's caller hands it — on the stand whole Timer ticks — while `click`, `type` and `press` leave the clock. The Timer state written through that step is what the registry's link 3 records once the stand's signals move onto it; the graph read must, like `click`, move no clock.

**2026-10-18-one-virtual-clock** — (the harness drives animation from the documents' clock) `advance` moves the `VirtualClock` by exactly its `ms` and the app's own time together; `click`, `type` and `press` leave it where it was (fct-e2e2e6vg / fct-za7xpowz). Recording the Timer's writes in the registry must not change by how much or when that state moves, and the new verb advances no clock.

**2026-10-18-engine-debts** — (the PROVISIONAL batch ratified by the founder, Epoch 2 close) ratified the `contain: paint` stop, the one-virtual-clock `advance` reading and the cursor fix. The clock and cursor facts the cascade binds this chunk to are ratified, not provisional.

**2026-10-20-load-wait** — (the load wait moves no clock) while an acting step waits on a load in flight for at most `LOAD_WAIT`, the `VirtualClock` stands still. Another «moves no clock» rule beside `advance`; the graph read on the `load` task must keep it.

**2026-10-31-engine-debts** — (the Cells grid's into-view move carries no animation) the Cells arrow keys' handler calls `MountedData::scroll_to(ScrollBehavior::Instant)` synchronously; the async form (a task spawned from a key handler) panicked `RefCell already borrowed` and did not ship. Moving the Cells signals onto the registry must keep this handler's synchronous instant call, and it is a key handler, so alone it does not make a node read «reacts to a click».

**2026-11-07-mounteddata-buffered-render** — (render-time MountedData calls on every Dioxus document) a render is recorded into a mutation buffer with the document unborrowed, then replayed under one borrow, so render-time `MountedData` calls no longer panic; such a call acts on the document as the previous render left it. The graph reader walks the vdom (`element_id.rs`) and reads subscribers inside `VirtualDom::in_runtime`; it must hold to this borrow order and read the screen after the replay, not mid-render.

partial — the chunk paints nothing; design-system binds only the agent-read carrier the graph read answers on (cli/mcp output form) and the select-list row precedent for a sub-target owned by an element

- The graph read's answer on `escher-session` stdout must be one line of JSON per command, keyed by the driver schema's own words, and nothing else on stdout (per design-system §Surface: cli › Component Patterns, sec-f5ysaan4, fct-6fb4pz6c / fct-or2earye).
- The new verb's answer must carry no colour, no colour dependency and no ESC byte, and no code may test whether a stream is a terminal (per design-system §Surface: cli › Component Patterns, sec-f5ysaan4).
- The verb's exit status must stay within the ratified class table (`0` accepted · `1` refused · `2` usage · `3` session error) read from the schema's `EXIT_STATUSES`, adding no new exit (per design-system §Surface: cli › Component Patterns, sec-f5ysaan4).
- The verb's `mcp` tool must answer newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0 lines only, one line a reply, its tool result's text the JSON line (per design-system §Surface: cli › Component Patterns, sec-f5ysaan4).
- An agent-visible node keyed with an optional owner must keep the select-list row reading: a row of an open list carries its own `bounds` in the snapshot while the highlighted row is in no snapshot and no tree (per design-system §Surface: desktop-native › Tokens (platform-specific), sec-yfvfpbhy, fct-grd6lupt / fct-6br6qi3d).
- A sub-target served by its owner's handler must not change hit-testing: a row of an open select list is answered before the walk and a box clipping the select clips no row (per design-system §Depth Strategy, sec-z7dbidjj, fct-zdoz4c52).

- The `escher-session snapshot` / `screenshot` answer shapes (one uncoloured JSON line; mcp image+text blocks) are the template a new verb's written form and MCP tool follow (design-system §Surface: cli › Component Patterns, sec-f5ysaan4).
- Open select-list rows are today's only agent-visible nodes that are not DOM elements of their own — owned by the select, with own bounds — the nearest precedent for "agent-visible node with an optional owner element" (design-system §Surface: desktop-native › Tokens (platform-specific), sec-yfvfpbhy); whether the code models them so is research's question.
- The seven_guis checks' shared reader asserts no-ESC on every answer line and the shared `Speaker` on every mcp reply; a new verb's lines pass through them (design-system §Surface: cli › Component Patterns, sec-f5ysaan4).

- No colour, ESC byte or terminal test on any answer line or mcp reply of the graph read (design-system §Surface: cli › Component Patterns, sec-f5ysaan4); design-system §Anti-Patterns reads NO RECORDED INTENT and is not cited.
- No second stdout line or stderr chatter on an accepted answer (design-system §Surface: cli › Component Patterns, sec-f5ysaan4).

- design-system §Surface: cli ↔ security §Surfaces: a new verb, outcome or open value set on a ratified carrier is a boundary widening, the founder's fork; the carrier form here is design's, the widening call security's.
- design-system §Surface: desktop-native › Tokens ↔ a11y/snapshot: the "reacts to a click" boolean and owner-keyed nodes sit in the ratified snapshot carrier beside the select rows' `bounds` reading.
- design-system §Surface: cli ↔ tests harness: the shared no-ESC reader and `Speaker` assertions cover the new verb.

- The graph verb's CLI answer is exactly one stdout line of valid JSON with no ESC byte, status `0` when accepted, and the same piped or not (per design-system §Surface: cli › Component Patterns).
- The graph verb's mcp reply is one JSON-RPC 2.0 line with no ESC byte, asserted by the shared `Speaker` (per design-system §Surface: cli › Component Patterns).
- After the change, an open select list's row still carries its own `bounds` in the snapshot, the highlighted row still in no snapshot and no tree (per design-system §Surface: desktop-native › Tokens (platform-specific)).

**2026-10-06-headless-stand** — the headless stand's TaskShell mount: added `task_in_shell`, which mounts a task as `main#main > #task-shell`, `#task-header > #back-btn + #task-title` above `#task-body` at the pinned 800 × 600, scale 1.0, Light viewport. This is the mount the extract requires to stay unchanged after the stand's signals move onto the registry.

**2026-10-06-stable-element-ids** — the lean tasks' controls carry author ids that are their stable element ids, with no class, style, wrapper or order added and no CSS selecting by them. This is the origin of the attribute-only discipline the signal-registry migration must follow, and of the ids that link 1 (node to component) reads.

**2026-10-06-id-persistence** — CRUD rows were keyed by `{person.id}` and no longer by their index, so a row's id follows its person. Moving CRUD's signals onto the registry must keep these keys and this row identity, and any reserved virtual-node id form must not collide with the id forms they yield.

**2026-10-06-accessibility-tree-identity** — the stand's inputs were named by attributes alone (`for`, `aria-label`), and a markup probe confirmed the files differ only by those attributes. This is the precedent for proving that a stand migration leaves the markup unchanged.

**2026-10-06-id-stability-across-code-edits** — CRUD rows read the author id `crud-person-{id}`, and Home's cards read `task-card-{slug}`, as attributes only. This rests on the founder's rule that every element an agent can act on reads an author key. The graph's node ids and the reserved virtual-node form sit beside these id forms (author key, anchored path, component path, document path).

**2026-10-07-driver-session** — the session host became a consumer of the TaskShell mount. It adds no markup, id, class, style, wrapper or order, a held instance reads as a fresh boot, and the mount and viewport hold after commands. This is the baseline for checking that a graph read changes nothing.

**2026-10-10-driver-cli** — `escher-session <verb> … --session <dir>` over the driver's verb table, with the four endings: accepted (0), refused (1), usage (2) and session error (3). Any new graph verb must keep these four endings.

**2026-10-10-snapshot-states** — stand tasks state their role and state by attributes alone (`role="listbox"`/`option`, `aria-selected`, `aria-invalid`), adding no element, class, style, key, id or order. This is a precedent for a new snapshot reading that touches the stand by attribute only. The new «reacts to a click» field lands beside these role readings.
**2026-10-10-mcp-surface** — the `mcp` role exposes the verbs as tools and is a further consumer of the TaskShell mount that adds no markup. A new graph verb appears in its tool listing.

**2026-10-12-self-description** — added `escher-session help` and `describe()` built from fixed table text, the usage line listing the verbs, and `mcp` tool descriptions given as the verb's help plus its result fields. A new verb or snapshot field moves `describe()`, the help texts and the tool descriptions.

**2026-10-12-headless-screenshot** — `screenshot` was added as the eleventh verb on both surfaces, and its in-band image was a founder-ratified fork. This is the precedent for how a new verb is added (its position, answer line, refusals and MCP block) and for counts that every pin must follow.

**2026-10-19-visual-lint** (the gated part: `escher-session lint`) — `lint` was added as the twelfth verb (eight instance verbs), listed after `screenshot` in the `mcp` tools, with its step kept under `--record`. This established the twelve-verb table the extract binds the new read to. The same marker's earlier entry set the in-process clean lint reading of the stand at boot, the layout regression pin.
**2026-10-20-select-by-id** — dropped the visual lint's PROVISIONAL mark: the lint is in process only, as built. This is part of the lint baseline the extract uses as the regression pin.

**2026-10-19-session-recording** — `--record` keeps every call as a replayable check, and `help` and `tools/list` read the same with or without it. A new graph verb needs a recorded step, and its recorded answer bears on «values masked, never logged».

**2026-10-19-recorded-check-replay** — the recorded check keeps each answer, masked as on every carrier. This was a founder-ratified boundary widening. A graph answer kept under `--record` must stay masked (`MASKED_VALUE`).

**2026-10-20-load-wait** — the help texts of result fields are the program's fixed table text inside a ratified carrier. This is the precedent for the new «reacts to a click» field's help text in the schema, `describe()` and the tool descriptions.

**2026-10-20-large-screen-in-parts** — `snapshot --part` added a flag and paged answers, and the usage line opens `snapshot [--part <part>]`. The new snapshot field must also hold for paged snapshots, and a graph read of a large screen (Cells, 676 cells) may meet the same bounds.

**2026-10-25-cold-agent-bar** — the six served screens (lean four, Cells by `boot_cells`, the load page by `boot_load`) and the `start` enum. Some ids were re-pinned, and the flight booker became a select. This defines which served screens the migration of the stand's signals must leave unchanged, and which screens the graph read serves.

body:
Builds the UI graph (v030-05): one read that gives, for a held instance's current screen, each node, its component, its handlers, the state they write and the nodes that read that state.
Link 1 and link 2 are read by the dioxus-core vdom walk the stable ids already run (dynamic attributes, exact, mounted included); links 3 and 4 by a new escher-side signal registry in dioxus-native-dom that the seven_guis stand's signals move onto.
Adds the reacts-to-a-click reading as a closed boolean snapshot field (absorbing res-gvelrxja), moving NODE_FIELDS, the schema help texts, describe() and every pin that counts them.
The read crosses escher-driver as a new verb, outcome, written form, MCP tool and recorded step; values stay masked and no log site, span field or print carries a node, component name, handler, state or value.
Reserves a virtual-node id form, keys the graph on the agent-visible accesskit node with an optional owner element, and lets a handler on an owner serve sub-targets; no 0.4.0 capability is added.

body_fields.what: the pinned starting reading of the reacts-to-a-click field (0 on the lean tasks, Circle Drawer 1, Cells 676, both layout modes)

body: dioxus-native-dom's new graph reader, signal registry and snapshot field: they add no log site, span, field, print or env read, and they carry no node, component name, handler, state name or value into any log, field or print.
dioxus-native-dom's optional tracing feature and its existing debug logs in mutation_writer, which already record text-node contents and attribute values: the graph code must add no such site.
Masking: a state value or control value the graph carries reads masked as on every carrier, a password's or a file input's value as the fixed mask MASKED_VALUE.

escher-driver's command span: the new verb's call through Session::run opens the one INFO span command, whose verb field is the verb table's closed word. The eight fields stay closed words, bools and counts, and no graph content (component, handler, state, node) becomes a field.
escher-driver's tool_call span: the new MCP tool opens tool_call with only tool (its verb-table word) and ending (accepted, refused or error), and adds no other field.
escher-driver keeps its 2 info_span! sites and 0 events, and stand_act_spans keeps its eight fields, after the new verb and outcome land.

The new Outcome variant is written in one place, by Outcome::to_json, as a command's answer and over MCP as its JSON line. It derives Debug like the rest of Outcome, but nothing logs, fields or prints it with Debug.

escher-driver's recording module writes each answered call's arguments, digest and answer into the kept check through the crate's json writer, so the new outcome's answer lands there as a file at rest, never a log line, field or print.

host_log and mcp_log read a sink-installing escher-session host and its mcp role at trace into their assertions: with the new verb and tool exercised, they read 0 id, name and typed-sentinel needles under both builds, and the span counts stay one tool_call line per call.

escher's sink scrub: an escher_ target prints every field but the content-named set, an engine target only the safe fields, and every other target is dropped. Any closed span the new verb opens is judged pair by pair by that rule.

escher-driver's describe() self-description and the schema help texts are written as one line of JSON through the crate's json writer, never a log line. Their moved text for the new verb and field stays an answer only.

The seven_guis stand (seven_guis::stand and its tasks) installs no subscriber, reads no env var and prints nothing. Moving the stand's signals onto the registry keeps the silence census at 0 over stand.rs and the stand tasks.

The two seven_guis binaries, seven_guis_native and escher-session, run escher_telemetry::init. The graph read reaches stderr only through that sink, and the escher-session command line writes the read's answer as one line of JSON on stdout, never a log line.

body_fields.convention: each new or extended test check installs no subscriber, reads no env var and prints nothing, its readings going into assertions only, with the silence census reading 0 over the file and any shared module it reads
each new escher-driver or dioxus-native-dom module holds no tracing site, env read or print, and adds no log site, span, field, log field or env read
each new outcome or read type that holds ids, names or values is written by to_json alone as an answer and is never logged, fielded or printed with Debug
each new verb or MCP tool adds no span and no span field beyond command's eight and tool_call's two, each a closed word, bool or count

body:
Builds the UI graph (v030-05): one read that gives, for the current screen of a held instance, each node, the component that rendered it, its handlers, the state they write and the nodes that read that state.
Links 1 and 2 are read by the public dioxus-core vdom walk that the stable ids already run. Links 3 and 4 come from a new escher-side signal registry in dioxus-native-dom, and the seven_guis stand's signals move onto it. There is no Dioxus fork and no blitz-dom engine change.
Adds the reacts-to-a-click reading as a closed boolean snapshot field, which moves NODE_FIELDS (thirteen today), the schema help texts, describe() and every pin that counts them. It absorbs residual res-gvelrxja.
The read crosses as a new escher-driver verb (VERBS holds twelve today) with a new outcome, its written form, its MCP tool and its recorded step. Values the graph carries read masked, and no log site carries graph content.
Reserves a virtual-node id form that collides with none of the four stable id forms, and keys the graph on the agent-visible node with an optional owner element. A contract or boundary change this brings is the founder's fork, asked at P4.

The driver command schema: the new verb joins the closed static VERBS table, and its arguments use bounded argument kinds. Every call passes validate or validate_session, a typed Command or a Refusal comes back, and nothing public runs a Command that did not come from validate.

The widening rule for the ratified carriers. A new closed-value field (the reacts-to-a-click boolean) is not a boundary widening. A new verb's carrier content that holds an open value set (component names, handler event names, registered state names) is a widening, and so the founder's fork.

The stable element id and its four forms: author key, anchored path, component path and document path. The reserved virtual-node form needs a separator no current id can hold, so no id can make two ids equal. The id is computed on demand and written to no log, and no NodeId crosses a carrier or is kept between calls.

Value masking: a password's or a file input's value reads as MASKED_VALUE on every carrier, the snapshot, its text and diffs included. This covers any state or control value the graph carries, never the text, its length or a file's host path.

Logging of the graph's content: no log site, span field or print carries a node, a component name, a handler, a state or a value. The one command span per call holds fixed words, bools and counts only.

The escher_telemetry sink allowlist: escher targets have their content-named fields redacted, engine targets keep only the allowlisted fields, and records from other targets are dropped. Any new escher-target field the graph reader or the new verb emits has to fit this rule.

The driver session socket's bounds: one request line under a size bound, a closed grammar, bounded replies holding ids, names, masked control values, snapshot text and diffs, and no NodeId. The new verb's answer and outcome travel on this carrier.

The MCP server (serve_mcp): the new verb's MCP tool has typed arguments, then validate. Results are bounded, protocol errors use fixed codes with no data, and there is no print, unwrap, expect or panic outside tests.

The escher-session command line: the new verb is read through the closed command_line reader, with the four fixed endings and nothing the caller typed written back. It installs no subscriber and reads no environment variable.

Recorded and kept checks: the new verb's recorded step is read back only through the strict Check::from_bytes, with closed keys and schema-named arguments. Each kept check holds the masked answer. The two committed stand-Counter checks hold no name, typed text or host path.

The typed Refusal: a closed set of eight causes with fixed names and no String field. A refusal or outcome the new verb adds stays inside this closed, fixed-text form, and only the cause's fixed name reaches a log.

The panic paths in dioxus-native-dom: element_to_node_id unwraps, NodeHandle::node panics on a missing node, and event-data downcasts unwrap. The graph reader and the registry must take the option-returning paths (try_element_to_node_id, try_doc) and must not panic on a stale or missing id.

Driver input-handling bounds: no unwrap, expect or panic on anything a call supplies, and no clock read in the schema or its validation. An id that names no element, or an element that cannot take the call, is refused with nothing run.

The snapshot and diff carriers (DioxusDocument::snapshot, Snapshot::to_text, Snapshot::diff) gain the reacts-to-a-click field. A diff takes its values only from the snapshots, so masked values stay masked.

The trust boundaries of the local session socket and the MCP stdio server: owner-only and with no authentication. The client receives whatever the graph read carries out (component, handler and state names), and what the client does with it is the client's.

Dependency security: the graph uses only dioxus-core's public API (vdom walk, dynamic_attrs, Readable::subscribers, ReactiveContext::origin_scope), with no Dioxus fork and no new package in Cargo.lock. The cargo-deny audit leg runs over the resolved graph under --locked.
The engine-change carve-out: a change to blitz-dom for every document would be a boundary widening. The scope expects none, and the registry graphs only the signals an app registers.

body_fields.convention: Each new test's environment read (CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR, CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR, TMPDIR) stays test-only and is recorded in the plan's list of environment values read. The library and the escher-session binary read no env var beyond RUST_LOG.
Each new log line or span field on an escher target holds fixed words, bools and counts only, never content, and passes the escher_telemetry allowlist. The crate installs no subscriber.
Each new refusal or session error is written from a fixed table with no path and no caller-supplied text.
Each new verb, argument kind or MCP tool goes through validate, with typed arguments and bounded requests and results, on every carrier: the socket, the command line and MCP.

Each new test fixture or committed check holds no typed text, host path, name or secret. A check of any session other than the committed stand-Counter sessions stays owner-only and is never committed.

body: **2026-10-06-telemetry-bootstrap** — wired `escher_telemetry::init`'s scrub and fixed the eleven content-named redacted fields (`url` … `panic.payload`). This is the set the logging rule leans on: a new `escher_` span field outside those eleven prints as written, so no graph field may carry a node, component name, handler, state or value.

**2026-10-06-stable-element-ids** — added the stable-element-id reader: an author key only when non-empty, `/`-free and first in pre-order, else a `/`-bearing path, "so no `id` makes two ids equal", with no panic and no engine id or pointer. This is the guarantee the reserved virtual-node form (`{canvas element}` + `{virtual key}`) must keep.

**2026-10-06-id-persistence** — a keyed list row's segment carries its Dioxus key `{tag}[{key}]`, and a key never comes from a pointer, hash or process counter. This is part of the id grammar a new virtual-key separator must not be able to collide with, and the precedent that a new key value class inside the grammar is no widening.

**2026-10-06-accessibility-tree-identity** — the id leaves as AccessKit `author_id`, with a CARRY to assert that it never carries a `NodeId`/`ElementId`/pointer. Standing rule: any further consumer of the id beyond the platform API re-opens the row. Keying the graph on the accesskit node makes the graph a new consumer.

**2026-10-06-snapshot-model** — the snapshot became an in-process reader of ids and names, resolved through `get_node` and never by index. Its trap: a first wire form of snapshot data is a crossing for ids, names and values. That is the shape the graph read and its new snapshot field rest on.

**2026-10-06-id-stability-across-code-edits** — set the four tiers (author key, anchored `//`, component path, document path) and the three-way uniqueness argument the virtual-node form must extend. It also scoped "no `NodeId`" to the id and the snapshot, since `UnkeyedActionable` holds a `NodeId`. Its trap: a wire form must leave `node` behind, which bears directly on moving off `Target.node: NodeId`.

**2026-10-06-snapshot-state-fidelity** — introduced `MASKED_VALUE` for a password's snapshot value: never the text or its length. Its trap: the mask covers the snapshot only, and a file input's host path reads unmasked through the same reader. Any value the graph carries must pass the same mask.

**2026-10-06-compact-snapshot-serialization** — extended the mask to `type=file` (compared ASCII-case-insensitively; `""` / `None` cases), and Data Protection now states that the file's host path never reaches the snapshot or its text. Standing rule: the first command exposing snapshot data is a new crossing. This binds the graph's state and control values.

**2026-10-07-change-tracking-and-diff** — a diff takes its values from the snapshots only, so masked values stay `MASKED_VALUE` in a diff entry, with no `NodeId`/`ElementId`/`ScopeId` in `DiffNode`. The new reacts-to-a-click field rides the diff under this construction.

**2026-10-07-audit-corrections** — a Dioxus key that is empty or holds `/` is refused, falling back to the positional `{tag}:{n}` segment, and a unit test witnesses each refusal. The virtual-node form's separator must hold against this segment grammar, and needs its own named witnesses in the same way.

**2026-10-07-driver-session** (socket vector; host-log reading) — created the owner-only socket (`0700` dir, `0600` socket, no handshake). Standing rule: a command carrying screen content reopens the crossing question. Trap: a "nothing in the logs" check over a process that installs no sink passes vacuously, so the graph verb's log check must run on a sink-installing host.

**2026-10-07-sink-target-allowlist** — the sink's three outcomes: engine targets print safe fields only, `escher_` targets print with the content-named fields redacted, and any other target is dropped whole at every level. `host_log` is the standing check against a sink-installing host. This is the rule a graph call's host-log read must pass.

**2026-10-07-command-and-refusal-schema** — created `validate` over a closed table: typed `Command` or `Refusal` in a fixed order, no `unwrap`/`expect`/panic/index on call input, no `Session` in its signature, and a refusal holding no `String` and no call content. The graph verb enters this table. The rule that no verb takes a wait argument or a wait result field starts here.

**2026-10-07-act-by-id** — `Session::run` validates first, and nothing public runs a `Command` that did not come from `validate`. Ids are looked up anew on every call through `get_node`, never by index. The graph read must take the same path and keep no `NodeId` between calls.

**2026-10-07-refusal-detection** — a sixth verb (`scroll`) widening the validated surface was ratified by the founder. This is the precedent that a new verb is a founder-ratified widening. It also added the session's private, bounded record of id text, never logged, and detected causes after `validate` in a fixed order.

**2026-10-07-driver-command-spans** (one span, eight fields) — one `command` span per call, holding only fixed words, causes and counts. Arguments, screen text, the record of ids and the outcome are never fielded. A graph verb may add no field carrying graph content without a new crossing question.

**2026-10-07-driver-command-spans** (the sink's second record class) — span lines print every field outside the content-named set, and a non-content span field's value is held in memory until the span closes. Any span field the graph adds would therefore print.

**2026-10-09-founder-rulings** — ratified the span record class and the diff's sizes in a log. Standing rule: a count of a diff's nodes may reach a log; no node, id, name or value may, and a field holding one is a new crossing question. This applies directly to graph counts against graph content.

**2026-10-10-driver-cli** (socket carries calls) — the socket's trust boundary was widened to carry calls and answers (ids, names, masked values, snapshot text, diffs; no `NodeId`), with wire grammar, 16,384-byte request and 1,048,576-byte answer bounds and `oversize`. The graph answer must fit inside this ratified crossing and its bounds.

**2026-10-10-driver-cli** (command line) — `escher_driver::command_line` is a closed reader: the call is checked by `validate`/`validate_session` before the session address is asked for, with four fixed exit statuses and nothing typed written back. Standing rule: every later surface's input passes `validate` first. The graph verb's CLI form reuses this path.

**2026-10-10-driver-cli** (ids, names, values leave) — ids, names and masked values leave in an answer, and `Refusal::to_json`/`SessionError` are written from fixed strings. Kept: no log, event or file carries an id, name, value, snapshot text or diff content. The graph answer extends this exit under the same rules.

**2026-10-10-snapshot-states** (the closed-field rule) — the founder's widening rule: a closed-value field inside a ratified carrier is no widening, while authored text, an open value set, a new carrier or a new exit still is. It put three closed state readings into the text/diff and the node keys. The reacts-to-a-click boolean is no widening under this rule; component, handler and state names are the founder's fork.

**2026-10-10-snapshot-states** (control-states row) — a closed in-process reader: values trimmed and matched exactly against a closed set, carrying no attribute text, with no log site or panic path even on a 5,500-character value, and exiting as closed enums/booleans. This is the pattern the reacts-to-a-click reading can follow.

**2026-10-10-mcp-surface** (MCP crossing) — the MCP server row: request and result bounds, fixed protocol errors with no `data`, the `id` echoed as the one client value, typed tool arguments refused `malformed` and then `validate`. Results reach the model provider through the client. The graph verb's MCP tool must go through this row; MCP was its own crossing question, and the next carrier is a new one.

**2026-10-10-mcp-surface** (`serde_json`, `tool_call` span) — `serde_json` is featureless and read-only. A second span, `tool_call` (`tool`, `ending`), was ratified as a new log field. The graph tool reads its arguments through that reader and adds no span field without ratification.

**2026-10-12-self-description** (`help`) — `help` became the tenth verb, a founder-ratified widening. The program's own fixed `'static` table text crossing the ratified carriers is inside them; text from a page, a call or a screen still widens. `differs` moved node keys from twelve to thirteen as a closed field. The graph verb's help, `describe()` and the `tools/list` descriptions are fixed text under this rule, and `NODE_FIELDS` moves again.
**2026-10-12-self-description** (session error table) — the `SESSION_ERRORS` table rows have fixed kind, meaning and remedy with no path. Any session error the graph verb adds joins this fixed table.

**2026-10-12-headless-screenshot** (in-band pixels) — the eleventh verb, `screenshot`. Pixels are no closed value set, so it was a founder-ratified widening across all three carriers under the unchanged bounds. This is the direct precedent for an open-content verb's answer being the founder's fork.

**2026-10-12-headless-screenshot** (causes, no image in a log) — a new cause joined the closed set as fixed text. A shot's content and size are never fielded, which needle checks on the host and the `mcp` role prove. This is the pattern for the graph's content staying off the log.

**2026-10-13-stand-keyboard-harness** — Enter/Space activation dispatches a Click through closed element-name/type gates, and `disabled` is read by presence (ratified). The reacts-to-a-click reading must agree with these click paths and gates.

**2026-10-14-stand-a11y-assertions** — the tree handed to the adapter is asserted headlessly: every `author_id` is its node's `element_id`, none empty, all-digit or `0x`. Keying the graph on the accesskit node rests on this proof that no `NodeId` form rides the agent-visible node.

**2026-10-14-quality-gates** — the audit is `cargo deny --locked --workspace --all-features check advisories licenses` over the whole workspace, with per-ID ignores only. A registry or graph reader using dioxus-core's public API must leave this audit green with no new package or ignore.

**2026-10-15-cold-agent-test** — the cold-agent check row: `valid_step` names `tool` by the verb count (then eleven, now twelve), at most 400 steps, closed keys. A graph verb must join that verb list or be stated outside it.

**2026-10-18-engine-debts** (`inert`) — `inert` is read by presence on an element or ancestor: such a node is not focusable, takes no hit, and its subtree is out of the adapter tree and the snapshot. The graph keyed on the agent-visible node, and the reacts-to-a-click reading, inherit this exclusion.

**2026-10-18-engine-debts** (`disabled` on form controls) — `ElementData::is_disabled` is presence on a form control only, read by focusability, `ClickTarget::Disabled`, `handle_click`'s walk gate and the activation arms, so a disabled ancestor `div` stops no walk. The reacts-to-a-click field's disabled reading must agree with this or name the fork.
**2026-10-18-one-virtual-clock** — `time-unavailable` retired, so the cause set is closed at eight. A graph refusal must fall among these eight in the fixed order.

**2026-10-19-session-recording** (kept check, reader, `--record`) — the recording directory (`0700`/`0600`, bounds) and the strict `Check::from_bytes` (closed keys, `malformed`, no panic, replay through `call_of`/`validate`). A call no record can spell is not kept. A masked `type` is kept as `MASKED_STAND_IN`. The kept check became the id's fourth exit. A graph step is recorded, or stated unrecorded, under these rules.

**2026-10-19-session-recording** (wire v3, session errors) — wire `v3` and `SESSION_ERRORS` at 15. `serde_json` also reads kept checks while writing nothing. The counts a graph verb's carriers and any new session error would move.

**2026-10-19-recorded-check-replay** — each kept answer is held whole, masked as on every carrier. The committed `counter-cli.json` / `counter-mcp.json` hold no typed text, host path, name or secret, are read only by `Check::from_bytes`, and are compared byte for byte with a fresh recording. The reacts-to-a-click field changes their snapshot text, so they must be re-recorded under these rules.

**2026-10-19-visual-lint** (in-process reader) — `Session::lint` was first a PROVISIONAL in-process reader of the id that "crosses nothing", returning ids, closed words and numbers with no `NodeId`. This is the precedent for building a graph reader in process before its verb.

**2026-10-19-visual-lint** (the `lint` verb) — the twelfth verb and eighth instance verb, a founder-ratified widening onto every carrier at once: the socket, CLI, MCP `tools/list`, the cold-agent verb set, the recorder's instance verbs and the kept check. Its content is never fielded, and `host_log` / `mcp_log` drive it with 0 needles. This is the exact template for adding the graph verb.

**2026-10-20-large-screen-in-parts** — the seventh argument kind (`part`) moved the arguments count. A part's number, count and text are never fielded, with needle checks on both logs. This is the precedent for any argument or paging the graph verb takes, and for the counts the schema row states.

**2026-10-24-stand-requirement-sweep** — `host_log` became a standing check reading a recording session's clients at `trace` with 0 id, name, sentinel and recording needles. The graph verb's no-log acceptance should extend this check.

**2026-10-25-capability-statement** — reconciled the carried sets on every carrier, and `docs/capabilities.md` states the MCP crossing's carried set as a pinned statement. If graph content is ratified onto MCP, this statement and its sites must name it.

**2026-10-25-cold-agent-bar** (the live child's kept checks) — the cold-agent pipe is a second reader of kept checks, holding bools and counts only, and its verdict fields are counts and closed words. A graph step's kept answer would sit at rest there and must stay unprinted.

**2026-10-25-cold-agent-bar** (six slugs, flight booker) — the flight booker's `select#flight-type` writes `flight_type` by a closed match over its two options. Moving the stand's signals onto the registry must keep this and the 7GUIs validations.

**2026-10-31-engine-debts** (Cells' `cells-grid` keys) — `cells-grid` takes `tabindex` 0 and a role-less `onkeydown` with a closed key match, clamped, and a click inside an open editor returns early. These are the role-less handlers the reacts-to-a-click reading (Cells 676) and the registry move touch.

**2026-10-31-select-popup** (what else of the list crosses) — an open row's `bounds` is a closed field inside the ratified crossing, so no widening. `NodeState` holds no field for it, `NODE_FIELDS` stays thirteen, and no `expanded` node key stands (the operator's call). This is the latest precedent and count the reacts-to-a-click field moves.

**2026-10-31-select-popup** (the select list in the log) — `packages/escher-driver/src` holds two `info_span!` and `stand_act_spans` reads eight span fields; page text reaches no log under host or role. The graph verb must keep these counts or re-pin them.

**2026-11-01-upstream-sync-ui-graph** (mounted event of a removed element) — `flush_queued_mounted_events` skips a removed element through the option-returning `try_element_to_node_id`. The graph reader and the registry resolve elements the same way, so a stale element is skipped and never panics. The sync was named for this chunk.

**2026-11-04-dioxus-runtime-probe** (MountedData hazard) — re-measured the `RefCell already borrowed` panic from a task polled inside `render_immediate`, and pinned it. This is the probe chunk whose measured mechanisms (vdom walk, `subscribers()`) the scope rests on, and whose `dioxus_runtime_probe` link 1 reads.
**2026-11-04-dioxus-runtime-probe** (zip ignores, nine) — the ignore count is nine, by ID with written reasons. The audit must stay at nine with no ignore added by the registry or graph work.

**2026-11-04-dioxus-runtime-probe** (advisories after a green audit) — standing rule: CI's audit can go red on new advisories over an unchanged lock, so run `bash .github/scripts/ci-leg.sh audit` locally before a push.

**2026-11-07-mounteddata-buffered-render** (buffered render) — `initial_build` / `poll` render into `MutationBuffer` unborrowed, then replay and flush. A registry hook or graph read inside `dioxus-native-dom` runs on this render path and must not reintroduce a borrow across `render_immediate`.

**2026-11-07-mounteddata-buffered-render** (recorder silence) — `MutationBuffer` has no panic path and no log site, print or env read, and its `Debug` prints `len` alone. This is the latest precedent in `dioxus-native-dom` for a new in-process holder of page content: the registry and the graph reader follow the same silence.

**2026-11-07-mounteddata-buffered-render** (limit for a task polled during render) — a task polled during render acts on the previous render's document. This is an open residual: a registry write recorded in such a task, or a reader resolving a node created in the same render, meets this limit.

relevant: the graph read crosses the ratified driver carriers (session socket, CLI, MCP stdio, recorded checks), adds a snapshot field, reserves a new stable-id form and carries state values, so the widening, validation, masking and logging rules all bind it.

- Widening rule: per security-plan §Input Validation (driver session socket, the widening rule), a new field of a closed value set inside an already ratified carrier is not a boundary widening, and a field holding authored text, an open value set, a new carrier or a new exit is one. The «reacts to a click» boolean in the snapshot and diff therefore falls on the not-widening side. A graph verb whose answer carries component names, handler event names or registered state names (open value sets) falls on the widening side, which makes it the founder's fork at P4. Whether the graph's content is closed or open is a planning question.
- Command schema: per security-plan §Input Validation (driver command schema), a new graph verb enters the closed `'static` table that `validate` checks (twelve verbs and seven bounded argument kinds today), and its refusals use the fixed order. Nothing public may run a `Command` that did not come from `validate`, and the socket, the command line and MCP all go through it. Nothing a call supplies may reach `unwrap`, `expect` or a panic, and no `NodeId` may be kept between calls.
- Stable element id: per security-plan §Input Validation (markup attributes, the stable element id), no HTML `id` may be able to make two ids equal, and no `NodeId` crosses any carrier. The reserved virtual-node form (`{canvas element}` + `{virtual key}`) must keep that guarantee against all four current forms. Keying the graph on the agent-visible node must not let a `NodeId` (`Target.node`) leave escher.
- Masking: per security-plan §Input Validation (markup attributes, masked values), a password's or file input's value reads as the fixed `MASKED_VALUE` on every carrier, never as its text, its length or a file's host path. Per security-plan §Data Protection (local user data handled), a file input's value holds a full host path that must not reach the snapshot, its text or a diff. Any state or control value the graph carries falls under both rules.
- Logging: per security-plan §Logging & Monitoring (escher's own sink), `escher_telemetry::init` redacts the content-named fields of `escher_` targets and drops records from non-allowlisted targets. Per security-plan §Input Validation (driver command schema), the one `command` span per call holds fixed words, bools and counts only, never a call's content. So no new log site, span field or print may carry a node, component name, handler, state or value, and the crate installs no subscriber and reads no env var.
- Recorded checks: per security-plan §Input Validation (recorded check), a recorded graph step is read by the strict, bounded `Check::from_bytes` (closed keys, schema-named arguments, anything else refused `malformed`, no panic path), and a replayed step still passes `validate` inside `Session::run`. Per security-plan §Data Protection (files, committed checks), a committed check holds no typed text, host path, name or secret.
- Refusals: per security-plan §Error Handling (escher-driver's command refusal), a refusal of the new verb is a typed `Refusal` from the closed cause set, with a fixed name, meaning and remedy, no `String` field and no path. MCP protocol errors use fixed codes and messages with no `data`.

- Closed in-process readers: per security-plan §Input Validation (markup attributes), ARIA states and closed values are read through closed parses that carry no attribute text, with no log site and no panic path. The «reacts to a click» reading can follow the same shape.
- `MASKED_VALUE` / `MASKED_STAND_IN`: per security-plan §Input Validation (markup attributes, masked values), every carrier applies the same masking, including the snapshot, its text, diffs and kept checks.
- Bounded MCP results: per security-plan §Input Validation (MCP server), tool arguments are typed and then passed to `validate` / `validate_session`, results are bounded, and the request `id` is the one client-sent value written back.
- One gate for all carriers: per security-plan §Input Validation (CLI arguments, escher-session), `escher_driver::command_line` checks a call through `validate` before it asks for the session address. A new verb's CLI form reuses that path and its four fixed exit statuses.

- Per security-plan §Input Validation (driver command schema): never let a graph read run outside `validate` / `Session::run`, and never `unwrap`, `expect` or panic on anything a call supplies.
- Per security-plan §Error Handling (escher-driver's command refusal): never put a `String` or anything a call supplied into a `Refusal` or a `SessionError`.
- Per security-plan §Threat Model Summary (local stdio, the driver's MCP server): never assume a result stays local. What a client does with a result, sending it to a model provider included, is the client's, so the graph must carry no unmasked value.

- obs: the escher-telemetry content-named field set and allowlist (security-plan §Logging & Monitoring) bind to obs's redaction rules for any new `escher_` span or event.

body:
Builds the UI graph (v030-05): one read that gives, for the current screen of a held instance, each node, the component that rendered it, its handlers, the state they write and the nodes that read that state.
Link 1 by the dioxus-core vdom walk the stable ids run; link 2 by the walk's dynamic attributes, `mounted` included; links 3 and 4 through a new escher-side signal registry in dioxus-native-dom, the seven_guis stand's signals moved onto it.
Adds the closed boolean «reacts to a click» snapshot field, absorbing res-gvelrxja: NODE_FIELDS moves past thirteen and the stand_non_lean_tasks starting reading moves.
Values the graph carries read masked as on every carrier, and no log site, span field or print carries a node, component, handler, state or value.
Reserves a virtual-node id form that collides with none of the four id forms, keys the graph on the agent-visible node with an optional owner element, and lets an owner's handler serve sub-targets, producing no virtual node.

body: dioxus-native-dom unit tests of the snapshot builder, its text form, its parts and its diff, and of the stable element id: the new graph reader, the signal registry and the new snapshot field each get unit tests there.

The NODE_FIELDS count (thirteen today), the schema's help texts, describe() and every pin that counts the snapshot's node fields move together with the new boolean field, in the snapshot and diff carriers.

The element_id unit-test pattern: build a DioxusDocument from a plain fn app, re-render by flipping a signal inside vdom.in_runtime, and resolve(0.0) through inner_mut() before reading a snapshot; the default config's no-op HTML parser means parsed markup is pinned in blitz-tests.
The bridge tests' rule: no function under test gains a constructor, a pub or a cfg(test) shim for a test's sake; private module state is reached by a cfg(test) child module.

The seven_guis headless stand (stand::boot, boot_cells, boot_load, boot_timer with TimerTicks, stand::options): the stand's signals move onto the registry, and every stand check over those tasks must stay green in both layout modes.

The shared stand tables and helpers in tests/blitz-tests/tests/common/mod.rs, session_common/mod.rs and fixtures/mod.rs: stated expectation, never a second mapping; a fixture page more than one check reads joins fixtures/mod.rs.

escher-driver's verb schema, JSON forms, MCP tools, recording and replay unit tests, and the twelve-verb count wherever it is pinned (VERBS, the MCP tool set, the cold-agent isolation check, test_capability_statement over docs/capabilities.md and README.md), should the read cross as a new verb or outcome.

escher-driver depends on nothing that names a virtual DOM, so its unit tests cannot build a held instance: how the read is asked and answered is checked by integration checks over a Session booted through the stand.

Session ↔ held instance: a call through Session::run returns after settle with the diff; a refused call leaves the instance unchanged and echoes none of the bytes it supplied; a password never leaves in an answer.

Masking: a state or control value the graph carries reads MASKED_VALUE for a password or file input, as on every carrier, read by the stand checks that hold a secret (stand_mcp_masked and the per-file SECRET checks).

Log scrub: escher-telemetry's target allowlist and redaction; host_log, mcp_log and stand_act_spans read 0 id, name and typed-text needles at trace under both builds; the driver's one escher_driver line per call holds fixed words and counts only; a new verb is a word of the command span's verb and tool_call's tool closed sets, with no span field added.
Engine features by runner: workspace and -p blitz-tests builds differ (tracing, writing-mode), so a check reading a sink's capture counts lines by target, never in total.
Recorded-check replay: committed checks under tests/blitz-tests/checks/ stay byte-equal to what escher-session records; a new recorded step form must keep them fresh.

Coverage floors in the coverage leg: packages/dioxus-native-dom 83 %, packages/escher-driver 97 %, packages/blitz-test-harness 90 %, keyboard_compat.rs excluded; the new reader and registry code count toward them.

The stand-repeat leg's zero-failure budget: the stand_*.rs files, the seventeen named blitz-tests targets and seven_guis' process checks run three rounds with no retry; a new non-stand_ target that must repeat joins that named list.

The agent-run proof counts: run stand (237 · 0 · 7 over 51 files) and run all (743 · 0 · 12) are re-counted with the chunk's new tests, a new stand_ file picked up by its prefix with no script change.
The headless-stand font rule: the stand checks assert unconditionally under the bundled DejaVu Sans with system fonts off, with no skip path.

body: **2026-10-06-stable-element-ids** (stand element-id checks counted; element_id unit tests) — set the `element_id` unit-test construction: a `DioxusDocument` from a plain app, re-rendered by a `GlobalSignal` flipped in `vdom.in_runtime`; a new `stand_` file picked up by prefix in `run stand`. The graph reader and registry unit tests must follow this construction, and link 1 reads through this id walk.

**2026-10-06-snapshot-model** (snapshot checks counted; dioxus-native-dom unit tests re-counted) — added the rule that `snapshot` unit tests call `resolve(0.0)` through `inner_mut()` after `initial_build`. Standing practice: each count is appended as a dated link and earlier links are kept as history. The new snapshot field's unit tests and the crate's count move follow this.

**2026-10-06-snapshot-state-fidelity** (state checks counted; unit-level route for a `disabled` pin) — the snapshot `build` helper carries a no-op HTML parser, so unit tests write attributes through `DocumentMutator` and parsed markup is pinned in blitz-tests. Trap: a headless deleting key is compiled out on macOS, so prove a state change with clicks and typed characters. This binds the graph's link-3 witnesses (a handler's write).

**2026-10-06-compact-snapshot-serialization** (text form tests) — introduced `Snapshot::to_text`'s unit tests (state tokens and their fixed order), `stand_snapshot_text` under `SNAPSHOT_TEXT_BUDGET` (10,000 bytes) and the in-file ceilings. Trap: a search for `snapshot.rs:` also matches `stand_snapshot.rs:`, so anchor citation searches on the path. The new field's text token and its re-measured screen sizes land here.

**2026-10-07-change-tracking-and-diff** (changed-set and diff coverage) — added `Snapshot::diff` unit tests over hand-built snapshots and `stand_diff`, where every step is held against the file's own reading of the two snapshots in both layout modes. The «reacts to a click» field becomes a diff reading that these checks must hold.

**2026-10-07-audit-corrections** (bridge tests, the shared stand module) — the bridge tests are a `cfg(test)` child module of `dioxus_document` because the handler's fields are private and it has no constructor. This is the precedent for reaching private state with no `pub` or constructor added for tests (dioxus-core hooks are `pub(crate)`). It also created `tests/common/mod.rs` with the `controls` / `rendered` tables as stated expectation. Trap: a sed or grep address that ends at a function's name also selects every item whose name starts with it.

**2026-10-10-snapshot-states** (driver-action census; counts re-read) — the precedent for adding snapshot node readings (selected / pressed / invalid). The dioxus-native-dom unit count and the builder, text and diff splits moved together, the Crud boot text moved 2034 → 2049 bytes, and the hosted snapshot line sizes were re-measured. The «reacts to a click» field moves the same set of figures.

**2026-10-10-snapshot-states** (what the new and extended checks assert) — `stand_snapshot_state` asserts that every node's state readings equal its accessibility node's, and that no other node reads them, in both modes. This is a precedent for a stand check asserting a new field per node against the accesskit tree.

**2026-10-12-self-description** (the self-description's checks and counts) — added thirteen node keys with help, `differs` in `Reading::ALL` order, describe.rs and its count row, `help` answering equal to `describe()`, and `stand_mcp_masked`. The new node field moves `NODE_FIELDS` past thirteen, the node-key help, the describe count row and `differs`.

**2026-10-12-headless-screenshot** (harness and session contracts gain the shot) — the precedent for a new verb. `screenshot` joined `command.verb` and `tool_call.tool` with no span field added (in step with obs-plan §4), the verb table, MCP listing, `cli_commands`, `mcp_server`, `stand_mcp_tools` and the session-lifecycle key all moved, and the carriage was the founder's fork.
